records.title: CVE-2026-116779, FreeSWITCH 1.11.2 and earlier: one inbound SIP MESSAGE can select the api chat proto and run FreeSWITCH API commands, the vendor says exploitation has been observed, CISA lists it as exploited, and 1.11.3 fixes it (CVSS 3.1 9.8)
records.headline: FreeSWITCH: one SIP MESSAGE runs API commands; vendor and CISA say exploited; fixed in 1.11.3
records.summary: SignalWire's advisory of 2026-10-28 describes CVE-2026-116779 (CVSS 3.1 9.8): an inbound SIP MESSAGE to a FreeSWITCH SIP profile selects the api chat proto and runs FreeSWITCH API commands with the privileges of the FreeSWITCH process, in the default configuration of 1.11.2 and earlier, and the advisory states that exploitation of this path has been observed in the wild. BSI CERT-Bund relayed it as a critical advisory on 2026-11-04, and CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-09 on evidence of active exploitation that it does not describe; no source names an actor or victim.
actions: Upgrade every FreeSWITCH to 1.11.3, or until then set enable-chat=false on every SIP profile that does not need inbound SIP chat and remove directory users that have no password; on an instance that SIP peers could reach, rotate the SIP trunk and directory credentials stored in its configuration, because the advisory lists disclosure of configuration and credentials as an impact, the vendor says exploitation has been observed and CISA lists the flaw as exploited.

records.title: BluePhishing: Proofpoint's proof of concept turns a consent link for a third-party Entra agent blueprint into tenant initial access, with an agent-creation permission that Proofpoint says cannot be revoked
records.headline: BluePhishing: consent to a rogue Entra agent blueprint gives tenant access, and default users can soon create blueprints
records.summary: Proofpoint describes BluePhishing, a research proof of concept that extends OAuth consent phishing to Microsoft Entra Agent ID: a victim who consents to an attacker's multi-tenant agent blueprint gets a blueprint principal with an agent-creation permission that Proofpoint says cannot be revoked, and the attacker then creates agent identities, up to 250 per blueprint, that inherit the consented permissions, which Microsoft's documentation says neither the Entra portal nor Microsoft Graph shows. Proofpoint has identified no in-the-wild activity, and Microsoft 365 message MC1506733 says default Entra users will be able to create agent blueprints from November 2026.

records.title: CVE-2026-123218, IBM Aspera Faspex 5.0.0 to 5.0.19: a crafted message bypasses authorization and gives full administrative rights, fixed in 5.0.19 PL1 with no workaround; CISA lists it as exploited two days after IBM's bulletin (CVSS 3.1 9.8)
records.headline: CISA lists IBM Aspera Faspex 5 admin takeover as exploited; patch to 5.0.19 PL1, IBM names no workaround
records.summary: IBM's bulletin of 2026-11-07 fixes CVE-2026-123218 in Aspera Faspex 5.0.0 through 5.0.19, an incorrect-authorization flaw that lets a user craft a specific message to bypass authorization and gain full administrative privileges (CVSS 3.1 9.8); the fix is 5.0.19 PL1 on Linux, applied by patching the container images, and IBM lists no workaround. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-09 on evidence of active exploitation that it does not describe; IBM's bulletin does not mention exploitation.
actions: Patch every IBM Aspera Faspex 5 server on Linux to 5.0.19 PL1 by patching its container images (the faspex-core image must read 5.0.19, Fix Pack 1), portals reachable from the internet first, then review the administrator accounts, API keys and shares created since the server was reachable, because IBM lists no workaround and the fix does not undo an administrator takeover.

records.title: CVE-2026-120017, CVE-2026-89126, CVE-2026-76964 and CVE-2026-89103, SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP, Web Dispatcher and Gateway: four unauthenticated network flaws rated CVSS 10.0 in SAP's CVE records of 2026-11-10, published ahead of Patch Day; no exploitation reported
records.headline: SAP's CVE records list four unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 flaws in Web Dispatcher, ICM, Gateway and the ABAP SAML2 service
records.summary: SAP, acting as CNA, published CVE records on 2026-11-10 for four flaws it scores CVSS 3.1 10.0, reachable over the network with no privileges or user interaction: an authentication bypass in the SAML2 service provider of NetWeaver AS ABAP and the ABAP Platform that lets an attacker impersonate any user, privileged accounts included, under certain configurations, memory corruption in SAP Web Dispatcher and in the NetWeaver ABAP Internet Communication Manager that could allow arbitrary code execution, and a default access control list in SAP Gateway that treats an external attacker as an internal application server. The fixes are SAP Security Notes 3849308, 3778556, 3778530 and 3798345, which need an SAP login, and SAP's November Patch Day page was not yet published when the records were read; no record names exploitation or a public proof of concept.
actions: Pull SAP Security Notes 3849308, 3778556, 3778530 and 3798345 as soon as SAP's Patch Day page lists them and apply the kernel or support-package fix each names, starting with systems whose Web Dispatcher, Internet Communication Manager or Gateway ports are reachable from untrusted networks.

records.title: N-able N-central: a researcher published proof-of-concept code for 33 alleged unpatched flaws, among them an unauthenticated XML external entity chain to remote code execution, and N-able took hosted N-central offline and told on-premises customers to power servers down; no CVE ids yet
records.headline: N-central: 33 unpatched flaws with public PoCs; N-able takes hosted service offline, tells on-prem to power down
records.summary: An independent researcher published write-ups and proof-of-concept code on 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-09 for what Huntress counts as 33 critical flaws in N-able's N-central remote monitoring and management appliance, tested on pre-release build 2026.4.0.31, which chain into four exploits, three to remote code execution and one to root; one chain starts with an unauthenticated XML external entity flaw. On 2026-11-09 N-able took hosted N-central offline in the Americas, Europe and APAC and told customers who run it on their own servers to keep them offline until further notice; it reported no active exploitation as of 2026-11-09 15:15 UTC, a hotfix is in development, and no CVE ids, affected builds or fixed builds had been published.
actions: Take every on-premises N-central server offline now and keep it offline until N-able confirms it is safe, then apply its hotfix, whose build may carry the same version number as today's; ask each IT provider that manages your endpoints through N-central whether it runs a server on premises and has taken it offline.

records.title: CVE-2026-105133 / CVE-2026-105134, AhsayCBS backup management console: an unauthenticated authentication-bypass and code-execution chain exploited since 7 October to drop webshells and a cryptominer; Ahsay says its earlier patches were incomplete and ships hotfixes 10.3.4.45 and 9.15.2.70 through its partner portal
records.headline: Ahsay admits its earlier AhsayCBS patches were incomplete; the hotfixes are partner-only and CISA lists both flaws as exploited
records.summary: Huntress observed from 2026-10-07 23:20 UTC attackers chaining two AhsayCBS flaws, CVE-2026-105133 (authentication bypass) and CVE-2026-105134 (code execution as SYSTEM through the Replication Receiver API), against internet-exposed servers of the backup management console that managed service providers and system integrators mainly use, dropping JSP webshells and an XMRig cryptominer; Bitdefender MDR investigated three intrusions through the same chain, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-14. Ahsay now says its earlier patches v9.15.2.59 and v10.3.4.0 did not fully address the flaws, so servers on them are still exposed; the fixes are the hotfixes v10.3.4.45 (v10) and v9.15.2.70 (v7, v8 and v9), available only to partners with a portal login, and a server that was reachable before the hotfix needs a compromise check.
actions: Find every AhsayCBS server your organisation or your managed-service suppliers run, including those already on v10.3.4.0 or v9.15.2.59, and apply the hotfix v10.3.4.45 (v10) or v9.15.2.70 (v7, v8, v9) now, then reboot it; the hotfixes sit behind Ahsay's partner portal, so ask the integrator or Ahsay for the build, and until it is applied keep the management web interface behind a VPN or an allowlist of trusted addresses.

Compromise-check every AhsayCBS server that was internet-reachable since 2026-10-04 against the indicators Huntress and Bitdefender publish, an OpenSSH service nobody installed included, and against Horizon3's server-side checks (new .jsp files in served application directories, replication receivers created outside a change window, unexpected system administrator accounts), and re-image any host with a confirmed compromise from a trusted backup, because the hotfix does not remove a webshell or a persistence mechanism that is already there; a missing webshell file does not show a clean host because one family deletes itself, and the credentials stored on or reachable from the server, those held in AhsayCBS and in other backup software on the same network included, must be rotated.

records.title: PK Softech, software supplier of Swiss pension funds: malware and a data outflow at Publica, with the City of Zurich fund PKZH saying its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Bernese funds BPK and BLVK and Pensionskasse Post also reporting the supplier incident, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office investigating
records.headline: PK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had promised in writing to delete; Tamedia says Akira holds about 100 GB
records.summary: PK Softech AG, the software supplier of Publica and other Swiss pension funds, says unknown attackers used malware to reach part of its IT and that data must be assumed to have left; the Confederation headlined its 2026-10-08 release "data outflow confirmed", and the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating. Tamedia reports that PK Softech had confirmed in writing in January 2026 that it deleted Publica's 2019 migration data, which apparently stayed on its servers, and that Akira holds about 100 GB and demands ransom; Inside IT relays this and adds that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira took data, and Netzwoche relays that the authorities assume data on practically all current and former federal and federally affiliated staff left. Publica says personal data of insured persons has presumably left; the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich says its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Pensionskasse Post says personal data left, the Bernische Pensionskasse assumes more data left the supplier than first thought but can neither confirm nor rule out that its insured persons' data is among it, the Ticino fund IPCT says data of about 1,800 of its insured persons sat on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more, and other funds are still checking. The Federal Data Protection Commissioner, who opened a formal investigation against PK Softech on 2026-10-22, states that data of several pension funds, Publica among them, was exfiltrated. Publica's own newsletter of 2026-10-22 says the Akira group is being associated with the attack; the demand rests on the press reports. The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich has suspended its planned 2027 move to PK Softech's system, PK Softech cannot rule out that non-pseudonymised data was temporarily present in project work, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office has added the case to its criminal proceeding against Akira. The Pensionskasse der Stadt Zug, administered by Libera AG, said on 2026-11-09 that there is an elevated risk, not yet confirmed, that its insured persons' data left the supplier.
actions: Tell the helpdesk, HR and payroll teams of every body whose staff are insured with Publica (including the federal administration and the ETH domain) or with the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, which says data of its insured persons and pensioners was stolen, that AHV number, date of birth, address, salary and IBAN may now be known to criminals and must not count as proof of identity, and route requests that quote them, a request to change a payout account included, to a call-back on a known number; for staff insured with Pensionskasse Post, the Bernische Pensionskasse (which can neither confirm nor rule out that its insured persons' data left), the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT (which found data of about 1,800 of its insured persons on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more), the Pensionskasse der Stadt Zug (which reports an elevated but unconfirmed risk that its insured persons' data left), a fund administered or advised by Libera AG or the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse apply the same rule until those funds report the scope; also tell insured staff that cantonal police warn of investment-fraud calls from people who know their salary and pension details, which prove nothing about the caller.

If your organisation's pension administration, HR or payroll runs on PK Softech software, is being migrated to it or tested on it, or your staff are insured with Pensionskasse Post, ask the supplier or the fund in writing whether your data, test data included, was in the affected environment, project, test and migration copies included, and what it holds outside the productive system.

records.title: Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controllers compromised, with forced defrost at hundreds of French supermarkets, refrigeration failures at more than 115 shops in at least six more countries and first cases in Germany, and on 2026-11-02 altered settings in the cold rooms of the French blood service through a refrigeration supplier, and on 2026-11-05 the first publicly known cases in Switzerland; France attributes the 11 to 12 October campaign to the IRGC unit Shahid Kaveh; ENISA and Europol call for immediate action
records.headline: France blames Iran's IRGC for the October refrigeration attacks; Swiss cases (Köniz, Volg) are not attributed
records.summary: Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed to AFP a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026, a remotely forced defrost at hundreds of French stores, and on 2026-11-09 France's foreign ministry and the C4 crisis cell attributed that campaign to the Iranian unit Shahid Kaveh, affiliated with the Revolutionary Guard's electronic and cyber centre, CERT-FR calling its case a bundle of indicators. The French documents cover that campaign only: more than 115 stores in at least six more countries and the first German shops followed on 2026-11-02, the French blood service reported altered cold-room settings at three sites the same day, and SRF reported on 2026-11-05 the first publicly known Swiss cases, a Köniz butcher and three Volg stores. CERT-FR reports numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and of Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb; NCSC Switzerland rates the activity actively exploited but says the public information does not establish a common attack method or confirm exploitation of the Danfoss CVEs it lists, and ANSSI says controllers directly on the internet and weak passwords were exploited. CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA and DOT published a joint warning on refrigeration and cold-chain controllers that names no vendor. ENISA, the European Commission, Europol and the CSIRTs Network advised immediate action on 2026-11-04, and Ransom-ISAC's log of one Copeland XWEB Pro compromise shows 743 parameter writes in two administrator sessions.
actions: Find every Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controller, and any other refrigeration controller with a remote management interface because not every second-wave site's vendor is confirmed, in facilities you own or that a contractor manages for you and take its management interface off the internet now, restoring access only through a secure VPN or protected network (filtering to the contractor's source addresses is an emergency stop-gap, and CERT-FR asks you to check your insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink); an end-of-life unit that gets no fixes needs replacing, because a factory reset leaves it vulnerable and probably compromised again.

On every such controller that was reachable from the internet, check the whole configuration, defrost ranges, alarm thresholds and notification recipients included, against the intended one, verify the actual temperatures and test that alarms reach staff; for a Danfoss unit that may have been taken over, restart it or otherwise factory-reset it, restore access only through a secure VPN or protected network and reconfigure it for service, then update its firmware, set the security level to Strict and replace the default and any weak passwords, and on every Copeland or Dixell XWEB unit confirm the factory Admin password was changed and give each contractor a named account with an expiry date.

records.headline: SonicWall SSL VPN bypasses SAML MFA and CISA lists it exploited; upgrade Gen7 to 7.3.4-7013, Gen8 to 8.2.3-8015
records.summary: SonicWall's advisory SNWLID-2026-0014 of 2026-11-06 fixes CVE-2026-19868, an SSLVPN authentication enforcement flaw (CVSS 3.1 7.1) that lets a user with valid credentials for an alternate authentication method bypass SAML, MFA enforced through SAML included, on Gen7 firewalls up to 7.3.3-7015 and Gen8 up to 8.2.2-8015 when SAML is enabled for SSLVPN logins. actions: Upgrade every SonicWall Gen7 firewall and NSv that serves SAML SSLVPN logins to SonicOS 7.3.4-7013 or later and every Gen8 firewall and NSv to 8.2.3-8015 or later now, because CISA lists the flaw as exploited; where a firewall cannot be upgraded today, disable or delete its LDAP, RADIUS and TACACS+ authentication servers, the interim workaround SonicWall added on 2026-11-09.

records.title: CVE-2026-123158, OpenSSH Portable before 10.6p2 (*sshole): on Linux with musl libc and no PAM, a password of 257 to 1,024 bytes logs in to accounts whose password field is *; NCSC Switzerland issued an advisory (CVSS 3.1 8.1)
records.headline: CISA lists the OpenSSH musl password bypass as exploited; update to 10.6p2 or turn passwords off
records.summary: OpenSSH Portable 10.6p2 of 2026-11-05 works around CVE-2026-123158, a password-authentication bypass on Linux systems that use musl libc and run sshd without PAM, Alpine's default OpenSSH server and OpenWrt among them: a password of 257 to 1,024 bytes logs in to an account whose password field is *. NCSC Switzerland published an advisory the same day and rates exploitation unknown; Alpine shipped fixed packages for every branch back to 3.16. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-09, and GreyNoise records hands-on logins on its gridpoints from 2026-11-07 that ended in a dropped Python implant; Previdian counts 22 attempts from 14 addresses as of 2026-11-10 and SANS ISC's honeypots saw attempts from 2026-11-05, and no source reports a compromised production host.
actions: On every musl-based Linux host that runs sshd (Alpine, OpenWrt, Buildroot, Yocto), install OpenSSH 10.6p2 or the distribution's fixed openssh package and restart sshd, because updating the package does not replace the running server, and rebuild container and cloud images from a fixed base; until then set PasswordAuthentication no in sshd_config and restart sshd.

On each such host that allowed password logins while reachable, search the sshd log for an accepted password on an account whose password field is *, and check root's and the default alpine user's authorized_keys for keys nobody added and the init scripts for a service nobody installed, because CISA lists the flaw as exploited and GreyNoise saw both persistence steps.

records.title: CVE-2026-116606 / CVE-2026-111560, Barracuda Email Security Gateway: an unauthenticated configuration-import bypass chained with a root command injection, with watchTowr's detection tool public since 2026-11-03 and its full chain since 2026-11-05; patches are out and Barracuda now reports exploitation against a small number of organizations (CVSS 9.3 and 8.6)
records.headline: Barracuda ESG: Barracuda reports exploitation, Canada names CVE-2026-116606; update to 9.4.0.029 or later
records.summary: Barracuda's advisory of 2026-11-02 covers CVE-2026-116606, a pre-authentication authorization bypass in the Email Security Gateway (CVSS 9.3) that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker restore a crafted backup archive through the configuration-import function, and CVE-2026-111560, a command injection in the timezone field (8.6) that also affects the Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, Web Application Firewall and Web Security Gateway; chained, they give root. watchTowr Labs showed on 2026-11-05 that the chain needs no account, one unauthenticated request to the login handler reaching the restore function, and Barracuda changed its advisory the same day to say authentication is not required for CVE-2026-116606, only that the administrative interface must be reachable; watchTowr published a detection tool. Barracuda added on 2026-11-09 that it has identified exploitation activity affecting a small number of organizations, without naming the flaw, and the Canadian Cyber Centre says open-source reporting indicates CVE-2026-116606 is exploited in the wild. Barracuda names firmware 9.4.0.029 as the fixed build while the CVE record lists builds before 9.4.0.030 as affected.
actions: Restrict the administrative interface of every Barracuda Email Security Gateway, Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, Web Application Firewall and Web Security Gateway to trusted internal networks now, update every Email Security Gateway to firmware 9.4.0.029 or later, the build Barracuda names (the CVE record lists builds before 9.4.0.030 as affected), and apply Barracuda's patch to each of the other products (BNADC-16586 for the Load Balancer ADC and the Web Application Firewall, BNMA-32468, BNWF-60060, BNYF-24789), confirming that automatic patching is on.

On every Email Security Gateway whose interface was reachable before the patch, check its configuration for a restore nobody made and its timezone setting for anything other than a timezone name, because watchTowr's single unauthenticated request can reach both.

records.headline: IBM API Connect: hard-coded admin credentials and pre-auth code execution fixed in v12.1.1.3 and 10.0.8.13
records.summary: IBM's two security bulletins of 2026-11-05 for API Connect fix, among many CVEs, flaws that need no privileges at CVSS 3.1 9.8: hard-coded credentials that give a remote attacker full administrative control (CVE-2026-17360, v12 only), OS command injection and path traversal to arbitrary code execution, an authentication bypass through improper signature verification, token issuance for other users and missing authorization over tenants. Affected are API Connect V12 on-premises v12.1.0.0 to v12.1.1.2 (fixed in v12.1.1.3) and V10.0.8.0 to 10.0.8.12 (fixed in 10.0.8.13); IBM lists no workaround and no source reports exploitation.
actions: Upgrade every IBM API Connect V12 on-premises installation to v12.1.1.3 and every V10.0.8 installation to 10.0.8.13, those reachable from the internet first.

records.title: CVE-2026-117691, Keycloak SAML HTTP-Redirect signature bypass: a percent-encoded parameter name lets an unauthenticated attacker log in as any federated user; fixed in Keycloak 26.8.2
records.headline: Keycloak 26.8.2 fixes a SAML signature bypass that logs an unauthenticated attacker in as any federated user
records.summary: Keycloak 26.8.2, released on 2026-11-05, fixes CVE-2026-117691 (CVSS 3.1 9.1, no privileges or user interaction): the SAML HTTP-Redirect binding processes percent-encoded parameter names such as %53AMLResponse while signature verification checks only literal names, so a crafted unsigned SAML message is processed instead of a signed one and the attacker logs in as any federated user. Red Hat, the CNA, names no mitigation that meets its criteria and fixed its build of Keycloak 26.6 in 26.6.9 on 2026-11-07. The release also fixes an unauthenticated JVM termination in the SAML 1.1 parser (CVE-2026-110931) and the bundled Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497, which CISA lists as exploited; no source reports exploitation of the SAML flaws.
actions: Upgrade every Keycloak instance that brokers a SAML identity provider to 26.8.2, and every Red Hat build of Keycloak 26.6 to 26.6.9 (RHSA-2026:96040; container images RHSA-2026:96039), internet-reachable login endpoints first.

records.headline: Microsoft: Storm-0940 runs ARTEX at machine speed; Mandiant now sees agent frameworks in incident-response cases
records.summary: Microsoft reports that since at least September 2026 Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, has used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework, to automate scanning, password spraying and OAuth-application abuse against hundreds of organizations across many industries including government, reaching privileged cloud access in under three hours in several cases; Expel saw the same infrastructure create its own accounts through Okta self-service registration. Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant report on 2026-10-31 that since late August they have seen ARTEX, PentAGI and CAIRN operated in incident-response cases, with ARTEX adopted by extortion groups and suspected PRC-nexus clusters whose victims include US government organizations, and that the original ARTEX repository was taken down in October while forks keep it in circulation. CrowdStrike and Recorded Future document another actor using the framework, and Seoul police referred a criminal group's leader to prosecutors on 2026-10-23 for extorting 38 of more than 90 organizations, with the same framework according to BleepingComputer. Microsoft adds on 2026-11-06 another cluster, the Cambodia-based, financially motivated Storm-3358 targeting financial organisations, and Check Point reads ten exposed operator consoles that show near-autonomous, opportunistic ARTEX campaigns. CERT-EU says AI-driven activity against the EU institutions it protects highly likely involved ARTEX.
actions: In every Okta org that allows self-service registration, review the accounts created since 2026-10-13 and every Okta Verify enrollment on them, and remove self-created accounts that nobody provisioned.

records.title: CVE-2026-61425 and the follow-up batch, Balbooa Gridbox for Joomla: a client-supplied cookie is accepted as proof of identity, giving anonymous Super User access
records.headline: Balbooa Gridbox for Joomla: anonymous Super User flaws exploited since July; update to 2.20.5.0
records.summary: The mySites.guru research campaign against Joomla third-party extensions produced six further disclosures between 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-23, and one of them changes technique class: the Balbooa Gridbox page builder (CVE-2026-61425) trusts a client-supplied cookie value as proof of identity, so setting an administrator's username in that cookie authenticates the requester as that user with no password and no existing session. A Joomla Super User can edit templates, which is PHP execution, so this is full site compromise from a single anonymous request. Fixed in Gridbox 2.20.1; the researcher says the vulnerable code shipped for at least nine months. The same week added unauthenticated SQL injection and order-forgery flaws in EasyStore, an invoice IDOR in Events Booking, and a critical unauthenticated upload in Membership Pro. A follow-up audit of Gridbox produced eleven more CVEs, fixed in 2.20.2, four of them exploited in the wild, and Gridbox 2.20.3.1 (21 September) fixes a further unauthenticated SQL injection present in every earlier build. Gridbox 2.20.4.2 (27 October) fixes two more unauthenticated SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 and CVE-2026-102789, with no exploitation reported, and Gridbox version 2.20.5.0 (4 November) fixes four more flaws, the worst an unauthenticated file deletion, also with no exploitation reported.
actions: Inventory Joomla sites for the Balbooa Gridbox page builder and update every one to 2.20.5.0, which also closes an unauthenticated file deletion and three further flaws fixed on 2026-11-04 and, from 2.20.4.2, two unauthenticated SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 and CVE-2026-102789, and the unauthenticated blind SQL injection in the front-end blog author parameter fixed in 2.20.3.1, present in every earlier build, 2.20.3 and 2.20.2.3 included. Anything below 2.20.2 is also exposed to the exploited follow-up batch, which 2.20.1 does not close.

On any site that ran Gridbox 2.20.1 or earlier while internet-reachable, review the Super User list and administrator-group members, remove accounts that entered an admin group through self-registration rather than an explicit administrative action, and review template files and the web root for changes, with particular attention to files written since 20 July, when the cookie bypass was disclosed.

records.summary: Synology said on 2026-10-29 that threat actors are exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 to encrypt and extort devices on outdated DSM, naming no CVE and pointing to Synology-SA-24:20, while the Chinese vendor 360 identifies the ransomware as C3RB3R, a Cerber variant, and says it got in through CVE-2026-13684 and CVE-2026-13639, the two unauthenticated CVSS 9.8 flaws of Synology-SA-26:13 (fixed in DSM 7.4-90075, 7.3.2-86009-4, 7.2.2-72806-9 and 7.2.1-69057-12, with no mitigation). records.headline: CISA lists WordPress core's upgrade-window RCE race as exploited; block wp-content/upgrade before installing 7.1.4
records.summary: WordPress 7.1.4 of 2026-10-28 fixes a weakness in the core upgrade process that lets an unauthenticated attacker reach the staged installer and run code on the server during a full-package core update, in versions 4.7 to 7.1.3, with backports for every branch down to 4.7. CISA added CVE-2026-119977 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-03; Wordfence reports more than 18,500 probing requests in the first 21 hours, while Patchstack calls the race hard to win and says it needs a web-reachable staging directory. The discoverer says the update that installs the fix still unpacks with the old code, so the staging directory must be blocked before updating.
actions: On every WordPress site your organisation, its web agencies or its hosting suppliers run, deny web access to wp-content/upgrade/ in the web server configuration (not with an .htaccess file inside that folder) and confirm it answers 403 before installing 7.1.4 or the fixed release of its branch, because the update itself still unpacks with the old code and a firewall that WordPress itself loads does not run for that request; then confirm in Dashboard > Updates that each site is on 7.1.4 or the fixed release of its branch.

records.headline: Sophos RCA: fake interview repo ran BeaverTail via VS Code settings; dead EDR agent, OAuth grant survived revocation
records.summary: Sophos discloses, as the victim, that on 2026-09-14 an employee cloned a repository presented as a job-interview coding assignment and opened it as a trusted VS Code workspace; its settings replaced the terminal profile, so opening a terminal downloaded and ran the BeaverTail loader and the in-memory InvisibleFerret backdoor on a Mac whose Sophos Endpoint agent had not reported since 2026-06-11. records.title: CVE-2026-98432, Linux kernel IPv4 TCP: a use-after-free in connection setup, present since 4.4, has an Anthropic-built remote root exploit against MPTCP listeners that CloudLinux could not reproduce; Citrix XenServer, XCP-ng, MikroTik, Red Hat, Debian, CIQ, Amazon Linux, Ubuntu 26.10 and Sophos have fixes, Ubuntu's LTS kernels are in progress and WatchGuard and Fortinet have none for their products (CVSS 9.8)
records.headline: Linux TCP use-after-free: Sophos Firewall hotfix and Ubuntu 26.10 kernel out; no fixed build from WatchGuard or Fortinet
records.summary: The Linux kernel CVE team published CVE-2026-98432 on 2026-10-15, a use-after-free in the IPv4 TCP connection setup path that dates to Linux 4.4 and is reached by a SYN packet carrying IP options; the CNA scores it CVSS 9.8. Anthropic reports that Claude wrote an exploit giving a remote, unauthenticated attacker root on servers with a multipath TCP (MPTCP) listener, which CloudLinux's kernel team could not reproduce; the Go team says the bug is not specific to MPTCP and Akamai that disabling MPTCP does not prevent exploitation, and no source reports attacks. Citrix rates its XenServer 8.4 and 9 bulletin Critical and names fixes for Workload Balancing and Conversion Manager, XCP-ng released a kernel fix, MikroTik's RouterOS 7.25.1 and 7.24.6 list the CVE, Red Hat, Debian, CIQ and Amazon Linux kernels are fixed, Ubuntu has fixed 26.10 while its LTS kernels were still in progress on 2026-11-07, and Sophos has shipped a Firewall hotfix and SD-RED firmware, while WatchGuard (Fireware OS, AP, Dimension) and Fortinet list their products as unresolved or under investigation without a fixed build, Fortinet offering an IPS virtual patch.
actions: On every internet-facing Linux server and every XenServer or XCP-ng host with its Workload Balancing and Conversion Manager appliances, install the vendor's fix and reboot as soon as it ships, then confirm the running version; Red Hat, Debian, CIQ, Amazon Linux, Ubuntu 26.10, XCP-ng, MikroTik, Citrix and Sophos (Firewall hotfix HF110626.1, SD-RED firmware 3.0.012) updates are out, and XCP-ng says that a host which cannot reboot at once should take its iptables-based mitigation first and the update later.

On hosts that cannot reboot yet, drop IPv4 TCP packets that carry IP options ahead of the TCP stack as CIQ, AWS and Vates describe, after testing on one non-production host because it also drops legitimate option-bearing traffic; disabling MPTCP alone does not close the path.

records.title: Exposed application credentials: Microsoft sees an agentic framework search GitHub for OAuth and cloud application secrets and then sign in as the applications from 2026-10-28, and Todyl sees an operator use MSP applications to reach 27 organisations, government clients among them
records.headline: Entra app-credential abuse: agents hunt GitHub for secrets, an operator reaches MSP clients, government among them
records.summary: Microsoft reports that since August threat actors have used the agentic framework ARTEX to query public GitHub for OAuth application secrets and cloud keys, and that from 2026-10-28 valid application credentials were used for service-principal sign-ins across dozens of applications in several tenants, a vendor-owned multitenant application among them. Todyl's telemetry shows one operator since 2026-11-01 targeting about 45 application registrations at MSPs, more than 33 of which authenticated, and reaching 27 organisations, government clients among them; Microsoft says a similar campaign involving the same addresses was reported by Todyl, and Todyl's update of 2026-11-06 now assesses its operator as an automated agentic credential crawler, likely fed by secrets exposed in public repositories or web apps.
actions: In every Entra tenant you run or manage for others, list the app registrations that hold client secrets, starting with multitenant, delegated-admin (GDAP) and Partner Center apps, security-tool integration apps and Azure DevOps service connections, and search the service-principal and non-interactive sign-in logs for the invalid-secret or expired-secret errors AADSTS7000215 and AADSTS7000222 followed by a success for the same app; on any hit remove all client secrets, certificates and federated credentials on that app, including ones you did not add, disable its service principal if needed and rotate everything stored in any Key Vault it could read, because issued tokens stay valid until they expire.

records.headline: Android 'SMS of Death': one hidden SMS drops calls, emergency calls included; Android 12 and 13 get no fix
records.summary: An independent researcher published a working proof of concept on 2026-10-29 for a zero-click remote denial of service in Android's telephony framework: one malformed WAP Push data message crashes the com.android.phone process, drops active calls including emergency calls and, because the message is retried, can leave a phone in a restart loop. Google's November 2026 bulletin lists CVE-2026-58882, the identifier BleepingComputer gives for the flaw, as a critical denial of service fixed at the 2026-11-01 security patch level for Android 14 to 17 (the researcher had named the October update); Android 12 and 13 phones run the same code unfixed, and no source reports exploitation.
actions: Move every managed Android phone below the 2026-11-01 security patch level to that level or later, phones of emergency-service and on-call staff first.
