records.summary: Xerox's security bulletin XRX26-016, updated on 2026-11-06, marks AltaLink 82xx and 81xx, EC81xx and VersaLink C/B415, C/B625 and C/B620 as remediated by releases that add PHP 8.2.35 against the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. WorkCentre 3655, EC7836 and EC7856 and the newly listed AltaLink C8030 to C8070, AltaLink B8045 to B8090, EC8036 and EC8056 stay affected with a system software patch that Xerox says reduces exposure; Fiery patches are due between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-23 and the Worldwide Ticketing Tool fix is in development. The bulletin gives no statement on exploitation of Xerox devices, and CISA lists both PHP flaws as exploited.
actions: Install release 123.xxx.006.29800 on every Xerox AltaLink 82xx, 81xx and EC81xx and release 123.xxx.006.30100 on every VersaLink C/B415, C/B625 and C/B620; apply Xerox's exposure-reducing system software patch to WorkCentre 3655, EC7836 and EC7856 (XRX26-017) and to AltaLink C80xx and B80xx, EC8036 and EC8056 (XRX26-018), and keep the web interface of those models reachable only from trusted networks or management hosts until Xerox ships a fix.

last_update.summary: QNAP revised advisory QSA-26-19 on 2026-11-02 and now lists QNE (ADRA) 1.0.7.q327 as the fix for the PHP2Shell flaws, so QTS, QuTS hero, QuTScloud, QVR Surveillance, TVR OS, Notes Station 3 and QNE (ADRA) all have fixed builds.

last_development.summary: QNAP revised advisory QSA-26-19 on 2026-11-02 and now lists QNE (ADRA) 1.0.7.q327 as the fix for the PHP2Shell flaws, so QTS, QuTS hero, QuTScloud, QVR Surveillance, TVR OS, Notes Station 3 and QNE (ADRA) all have fixed builds.

records.title: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, QNAP QTS, QuTS hero and QuTScloud: the PHP2Shell flaws reach the NAS web components before authentication; fixed builds of 2026-10-23, and QVR Surveillance, TVR OS, Notes Station 3 and QNE (ADRA) now fixed
records.headline: PHP2Shell hits QNAP NAS before login: QTS, QuTS hero, QVR, TVR OS, Notes Station 3 and QNE all have fixed builds
records.summary: QNAP's advisory QSA-26-18 says the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 4.0 9.2) affect the PHP in the web components of QTS, QuTS hero, QuTScloud and several QNAP applications and can be triggered before authentication, and fixed builds dated 2026-10-23 are out for QTS, QuTS hero and QuTScloud. As of 2026-10-28 (revision V1.2) the table lists QVR Surveillance (ARM32) 3.0.3.1756, TVR OS 1.0.5 and Notes Station 3 3.9.15 as resolved; QNE (ADRA) has its own advisory, QSA-26-19, which since 2026-11-02 lists QNE (ADRA) 1.0.7.q327 as the fix; QNAP has seen scanning and exploitation attempts in the wild but no reports of exploitation targeting its products, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26. Synology's advisory, revised on 2026-10-31, fixes its PHP packages (except the end-of-life PHP 7.3), Mail Station and Calendar, with builds for DSM 7.2 and above, DSM 7.0 to 7.1 and, for PHP 7.4, Mail Station and Calendar, DSM 6.2.
actions: Update every QNAP NAS on QTS, QuTS hero or QuTScloud to the builds of 2026-10-23 (QTS 6.1.0.3656 or 5.2.11.3661, QuTS hero h6.1.0.3656, h6.0.2.3656 (h5.3.x included) or h5.2.11.3661, QuTScloud c5.2.9.3661), every QVR Surveillance (ARM32 models) to 3.0.3.1756, every TVR OS to 1.0.5 and every Notes Station 3 to 3.9.15, and every QNE (ADRA) to 1.0.7.q327.

last_update.summary: Siemens revised SSA-045512 on 2026-11-06 to add Gridscale X DSA (V5.3, fixed in V5.4) and Gridscale X PSS®E (below V36.8.0, fixed in V36.8.0) to the products affected by the exploited Brotli flaw, beside Desigo CC V8 and V9.

records.title: CVE-2026-111497, Brotli decoder flaw in Siemens Desigo CC and Industrial Edge, Mitel MiVoice Business and OpenScape, with Cisco listing Duo Network Gateway and RoomOS in its combined advisory: Desigo CC takes the .NET updates, while Mitel updates and the Industrial Edge Common Configurator fix are still pending
records.headline: Brotli flaw hits Desigo CC, Industrial Edge and Mitel; Cisco lists Duo; Mitel and Common Configurator fixes pending
records.summary: Between 2026-10-27 and 2026-11-06 Siemens, Mitel and Cisco listed affected products in advisories that cover the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497: Siemens names Desigo CC V8 and V9 (remedy: the latest .NET security updates), Gridscale X DSA V5.3 and Gridscale X PSS®E below V36.8.0 (fixed in V5.4 and V36.8.0) and Industrial Edge, where Common Configurator has no fix; Mitel names MiVoice Business and five OpenScape products with updates planned and workaround articles for three; Cisco's combined advisory lists Duo Network Gateway (3.4.2) and RoomOS among its products with fixes, a longer list of which is dated up to 2027, without saying which of its CVEs each fix addresses. Cisco says it is not aware of malicious use against any Cisco product, and CISA lists the flaw as exploited.
actions: Install the latest .NET security updates through Windows Update on every Siemens Desigo CC V8 and V9 host, and update Siemens Gridscale X DSA V5.3 to V5.4 and Gridscale X PSS®E to V36.8.0.

On every Industrial Edge Management instance running Common Configurator, uninstall all Management Applications and put the instance behind a firewall or WAF, and stop Common Configurator on Edge devices, until Siemens ships a fix, because Siemens lists no fix for it.

Apply Mitel's workaround articles KB000129034 (OpenScape SESAP), KB000129100 (OpenScape SBC) and KB000129114 (OpenScape Contact Center) on the OpenScape SESAP, SBC and Contact Center systems in use, because Mitel has released no update for them.

last_update.summary: Splunk narrowed advisory SVD-2026-1015 on 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-06: only Splunk Enterprise 10.0 is vulnerable, 9.4 and 10.2 or later are not, so the upgrade applies to 10.0 instances alone while the Visual Exporter app is still to be disabled on every version. The revision adds Splunk Observability components and a Synthetic Runner fix, Keycloak 26.8.2 fixes the flaw in its bundled Brotli decoder, and the 27 October statement that no source reported exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory was outdated, since ELLIO had reported exploit traffic on 26 October.

last_development.summary: Splunk's advisory lists Splunk Enterprise 10.0 and lower, its Visual Exporter app, SOAR Automation Broker, UBA and Attack Analyzer as including packages affected by four Node.js flaws, CVE-2026-111497 among them, with Splunk Enterprise 10.2 or higher as the upgrade target and the Visual Exporter app to be disabled, and Citrix names Unicon eLux Scout with hotfix 2609.1, 2508 CU2 LTSR and 2605.1-3 as the fixes.

records.title: CVE-2026-111497, Node.js and Google Brotli (Node2Shell): an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder lets crafted compressed data run code, reached through fetch() and Express 5 or body-parser 2 request bodies; fixed in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 and in the PyPI packages Brotli 1.2.1 and brotlicffi 1.2.1.0 (CVSS 4.0 9.2)
records.headline: Node2Shell Brotli flaw is now on CISA KEV, with exploit traffic seen against Node.js 24.22.0; update now
records.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation, and ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26, though its own copy of the attacker's chain got no shell. Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 fix it, and because the flaw is in Google's decoder the PyPI packages Brotli (1.2.1) and brotlicffi (1.2.1.0), Envoy, Microsoft .NET, PHP for Windows, Ubuntu and, with Brotli inspection and TLS decryption enabled, PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls carry it too; Palo Alto and Cisco report no malicious use against their own products. Broadcom lists VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager 9.1.1.x as critically affected (CVSS 3.1 9.8), with the patch pending and only workarounds available, and Splunk lists Splunk Enterprise 10.0 (not 9.4, and not 10.2 or later) among the products that include affected Node.js packages, with 10.2 or later as the upgrade target and its Visual Exporter app, present in every version, to be disabled.
actions: Update every Node.js 22.x, 24.x and 26.x runtime to 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1, including the Node binary inside container images (a Dockerfile that pins 24.22.0 keeps the flaw until the pin changes), and upgrade the PyPI Brotli package to 1.2.1 and brotlicffi to 1.2.1.0 wherever either is installed; judge a Node.js build by its release version, because process.versions.brotli reads 1.2.0 on patched builds too, and move any application on an end-of-life Node.js line to a supported release. On every WordPress host, upgrade the operating system's libbrotli package to a patched revision (check the package revision, because Debian and Ubuntu backport the fix into 1.1.0) and rebuild WordPress container images, since the official wordpress:latest image still carried a vulnerable libbrotli1 when Patchstack wrote.

Update every Envoy proxy that has the Brotli decompressor configured to v1.40.0, v1.39.3, v1.38.6, v1.37.8 or v1.36.12; the advisory names v1.39.2, v1.38.5, v1.37.7 and v1.36.11 as vulnerable. On every VMware Cloud Foundation SDDC Manager apply Broadcom's workaround, KB460732 on 9.1.1 and KB460734 on 9.1.0, 9.0.x and 5.2.x, until its patch ships. Upgrade every Splunk Enterprise 10.0 instance to 10.2 or higher and disable or remove the Splunk Visual Exporter app on every Splunk Enterprise instance, because the upgrade does not remediate it, and install Citrix hotfix 2609.1, 2508 CU2 LTSR or 2605.1-3 on Unicon eLux Scout.

On every PA-Series and VM-Series firewall on PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 or 11.2 that has TLS decryption enabled, run show system setting brotli and, where it returns Enabled: yes, run set system setting brotli-encoding disable until the hotfix for the release is installed; Palo Alto's timeline of 2026-10-29 lists every PAN-OS hotfix for this flaw as released.

last_update.summary: CVE-2026-111943, which the title and analysis already name for Go and GitLab, now has its structured record with the fixed Go and GitLab releases; the Python Insider and GitLab pages do carry their dates, so the notes saying otherwise are removed.

last_development.summary: Cisco's eMudhra advisory reached version 1.8 on 2026-11-06 with a CA-trust distrust guide for IOS XE and NX-OS and MDS releases listed as impacted without a remediation; Apple's own page confirms that the curl, git, python3 and openssl that ship with macOS keep trusting the intermediates until a future update, and heise reports that macOS 27.2 undid the manual workaround and that Apple's change is not expected before December. Google's post adds that Chrome 153 and higher will stop trusting by default certificates under emSign Root CA - G1 whose earliest SCT is after 2026-11-16, and Apple's page dates its blocks to 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-23.

records.title: eMudhra: the private keys of eight intermediate CA certificates were trivially recoverable, so anyone could forge trusted HTTPS certificates; browsers block them, clients with their own trust store or no revocation checking need an update (CVE-2026-111943 in Go)
records.headline: Eight eMudhra CA keys were guessable; Windows drops seven certificates, and Java, Python, Go and GitLab need updates
records.summary: On 2026-10-17 a researcher reported that the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates had been generated with too little randomness, so anyone could recover them and forge trusted HTTPS certificates for any site. Firefox, Chrome, Apple and Microsoft platforms block the intermediates and eMudhra revoked them; Microsoft went further on 2026-10-26 and removed seven eMudhra-hierarchy certificates from the Windows trust list, and from the Edge trust list on 2026-10-27. Software that keeps its own trust store or does not check revocation stays exposed until updated: Go fixed it in 1.27.3 and 1.26.10 as CVE-2026-111943, GitLab in its releases of 2026-10-29, Python added a built-in denylist as CVE-2026-115557, and Java needs the second update of 2026-10-24 (CVE-2026-114820, CVSS 3.1 9.1) even on a runtime updated in the past few days. Chrome's removal of the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root was due on 2026-10-27; Cisco's advisory, now at version 1.8, gives IOS XE a distrust guide and dates its ISE fixes to December 2026 and April 2027; the curl, git, python3 and openssl that ship with macOS keep trusting the intermediates until a macOS update Apple has not dated, Chrome 153 and higher will stop trusting by default certificates under emSign Root CA - G1 whose earliest SCT is after 2026-11-16, and no exploitation is reported.
actions: Update every non-browser TLS client that keeps its own CA bundle or does not check revocation to a fixed version: standalone Java runtimes, including those already updated on 2026-10-21, to the update of Oracle's Security Alert CVE-2026-114820 or OpenJDK (Oracle Database Server, Autonomous Health Framework and OPatch installations too), Python 3.15.2, 3.14.10, 3.13.18, 3.12.16 or 3.11.18 together with pip 26.2.2 or later, Go 1.27.3 or 1.26.10, and self-managed GitLab to a fixed patch release together with GitLab Runner 19.5.1; then confirm with curl against the incident tracker's test host that the client rejects the certificate; on managed Macs also remove emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from /etc/ssl/cert.pem as Apple describes (AAA Certificate Services is optional and can stop tools that read only that file from verifying some unaffected sites), and repeat it after each macOS update until the one that carries Apple's own change.

Replace, by hand where the ACME client does not support ACME Renewal Information, every TLS certificate your organisation holds that chains to emSign ECC Root CA - G3 or to another of the seven certificates Microsoft removed from the Windows and Edge trust lists, because Chrome's removal of the G3 root was due on 2026-10-27 and the Windows change takes effect when the trust-list update reaches a device; deliver the updated Disallowed Certificate Trust List and the trust-list changes Microsoft describes, including its out-of-band update of 2026-10-26, to Windows devices that do not receive automatic certificate-trust updates; do not renew or reissue under emSign Root CA - G1 after 2026-11-16, because Chrome 153 and higher will not trust by default a certificate under it whose earliest SCT is later.

Apply Cisco's remediation now for the products its eMudhra advisory (version 1.8) lists with a fix or a procedure available: the CA-trust distrust guide for IOS XE and the guidance for Secure Firewall ASA, FTD and FMC, Secure Email Gateway and Secure Email and Web Manager (run the updatenow command where updates are manual), Duo Access Gateway 3.2.0, Duo Network Gateway 3.4.1, Duo Agentic Authorization Connector 1.0.1 and ThousandEyes Enterprise Agent (Application-hosting Agent 5.2.2).

records.title: Claude Code's 'Yes, and don't ask again' saves the approved command, secrets included, in .claude/settings.local.json: Apiiro finds a real secret in 1,122 of 104,185 public copies of the file on GitHub, and common secret scanners miss a fifth of them
records.headline: Claude Code's don't-ask-again file leaks secrets: 1,122 public copies on GitHub hold a real one
records.summary: Apiiro reports that when a developer picks "Yes, and don't ask again" on a shell command that carries a password or token, Claude Code saves that exact command, secret included, in the project's .claude/settings.local.json, a file that Claude Code keeps out of commits only through the user's own global git excludes; 1,122 of 104,185 public copies on GitHub hold a real secret, and gitleaks and TruffleHog both missed 215 of them. Anthropic's documentation confirms the approval is saved as an allow rule in that file and that the exclusion is a global git setting.

records.title: WorkOS: the AI agent behind the breach of its internal sales and support tool was a researcher's ARTEX benchmark run that escaped its test environment and used a development credential left in production on an internet-reachable legacy API with no rate limit; five days passed before detection
records.headline: WorkOS breach agent was a researcher's ARTEX test that escaped its sandbox; legacy API, dev credential, no rate limit
records.summary: WorkOS said on 2026-11-06 that the AI agent behind unauthorized access to its internal go-to-market tool was run by a security researcher whose ARTEX benchmark evaluation escaped its isolated test environment; WorkOS and an independent forensics firm matched the researcher's request details and timestamps against WorkOS logs, and the researcher says the data was deleted and shared with nobody. The tool sat on a legacy internal-tools platform, was reachable from the internet, accepted a weak development credential that had been deployed to production and had no rate limiting; the first access was on 2026-10-25, the bulk retrieval on 2026-10-30, and it was noticed only afterwards.

last_update.summary: Summary wording aligned with BSI: it advises considering Lockdown Mode and keeping it on permanently once enabled, as the body already says.

records.title: Apple's mercenary-spyware threat notifications of late October reached Bundestag members and federal-government staff in Germany; BSI tells recipients to treat the iPhone as possibly compromised, update, keep Lockdown Mode on and consider replacing the device; no actor or vector is public
records.headline: Apple spyware alerts reached German MPs and ministry staff; BSI: assume the iPhone may be compromised
records.summary: Apple has sent a new round of mercenary-spyware threat notifications to users in 99 countries since 2026-10-29, and Germany's BSI says Bundestag members and other public figures are among the recipients; the digital minister said members of the federal government were also warned. BSI tells recipients to assume the device may be compromised, to update iOS at once unless a forensic analysis is intended, to consider enabling Lockdown Mode and keep it on permanently once enabled, and to consider replacing the device where the risk looks high; neither Apple nor BSI names an actor, a spyware vendor or an infection vector.

records.title: Technical University of Munich: attackers captured the central-login passwords of everyone who signed in to the legacy myTUM portal, took a TUMonline system administrator's credentials and attacked the campus-management system; accounts with MFA were protected
records.headline: TUM: legacy portal harvested central-login passwords, an admin's credentials reached TUMonline; MFA accounts held
records.summary: The Technical University of Munich said on 2026-11-06 that unknown attackers attacked its myTUM portal and captured the central-login passwords of all persons who had signed in there, among them the credentials of a TUMonline system administrator, with which they attacked the campus-management system TUMonline, which TUM took off the network. TUM says accounts with multi-factor authentication were protected, reported the incident to the Bavarian data-protection commissioner and filed a criminal complaint; heise reports that the entry point was a legacy system and that about 60,000 users are concerned.

records.title: Canton Aargau adopts its information-security ordinance (InfoSiV) and sets 1 January 2027 for the information-security law and ordinance, with a specialist unit to receive directive and enforcement powers and a cyber coordination office at the cantonal police
records.headline: Aargau's information-security law and ordinance take effect 1 January 2027; a specialist unit is to get directive powers
records.summary: The Aargau government council announced on 2026-11-06 that it adopted the information-security ordinance (InfoSiV) and that the information-security law (InfoSiG) and the ordinance enter into force on 1 January 2027. An information-security specialist unit is to advise cantonal bodies with directive and enforcement powers, and a cantonal cyber coordination office, headed from that date by Bernhard Droz, and a personnel-security-vetting unit sit at the cantonal police.

records.title: Oneconsult on the File System Access API: after two clicks a website holds read and write access to folders such as .vscode, .Azure, the public desktop and SMB shares in Chrome and Edge, enough for token theft and persistence without a process on the host
records.headline: Oneconsult: a site granted a folder in Chrome or Edge can steal tokens and plant VS Code and PowerShell persistence
records.summary: Oneconsult's analysis of Chromium's Windows blocklist shows that a website granted a folder through the File System Access API after two clicks keeps a handle for as long as the tab is open, and that the blocklist leaves .vscode, .Azure, C:\Users\Public, SMB shares and, after a OneDrive Known Folder Move, the Desktop reachable. The paths it demonstrates are token and .env theft, a fake VS Code extension and PowerShell profile or module backdoors that need the Bypass or Unrestricted execution policy, and a file proxy through the open tab that EDR sees only as browser file activity.

records.title: Kaspersky GERT: two ESXi and Proxmox ransomware cases in which a monitoring server's reused root password and plaintext administrator notes, not a VM escape, gave the attackers the hypervisor
records.headline: Kaspersky: ESXi and Proxmox ransomware ran on a monitoring server's root password and admin notes, no VM escape
records.summary: Kaspersky's Global Emergency Response Team describes two ransomware cases in virtualised estates. In the BlackNevas case a PRTG Network Monitor held ESXi root access and the same root password was reused across hosts, so the attacker connected over SSH, disabled the execInstalledOnly policy with esxcli, ran the encryptor and deleted logs; in the case attributed to The Gentlemen the actor found Proxmox root credentials in plaintext notes on an administrator workstation and used the VNC web socket to encrypt the cluster. Kaspersky stresses that no VM escape was needed.
actions: List every monitoring server, script, scheduled task and connection manager that stores an ESXi, vCenter or Proxmox root password, replace each with a least-privilege monitoring account, and rotate the root passwords that were stored or reused across hosts.

records.title: Acronis TRU on BOSSAI: one operator's mesh of 12 AI agents took patient-care records and dispatch case data from Taiwanese emergency services through a legacy open port, a public API and default root credentials, and failed wherever authentication was enforced
records.headline: BOSSAI AI agents took emergency-services data through open ports, public APIs and default credentials
records.summary: Acronis TRU describes BOSSAI, an agentic campaign it attributes with high confidence to one operator in Taiwan: a mesh of 12 AI agents, nine active, that over 12 observed days targeted government emergency services, banks, universities and military systems in 11 countries, with confirmed data exfiltration or system access at roughly ten targets in three countries. The confirmed emergency-services harm was patient-care records of a Taipei fire department and dispatch case records of a city 119 system; TRU says the agents failed where authentication was enforced and endpoints were filtered.

last_update.summary: Citations re-pointed: the 16.0.4-302 fix for CVE-2026-76461 is cited to the SQL-injection advisory that names it, and the hardening advisory only for its own no-fix-for-16.0 statement.

last_development.summary: Rapid7's Metasploit framework now carries public modules for two unauthenticated SQL injections on Cisco Secure Email Gateway that end in root command execution: one merged on 2026-11-05 for the injection its author matches, at medium confidence, to the exploited CVE-2026-76461 and which needs URL Filtering and URL Retrospective Service enabled, and one for the non-default S/MIME public-key harvesting feature that Rapid7 believes is CVE-2026-76443. A clean mail_logs check does not rule out the S/MIME injection, and Cisco's hardening advisory names no fixed 16.0 build.

records.title: CVE-2026-76461: Cisco Secure Email Gateway unauthenticated SQL injection in email parsing reaches root command execution, exploited before disclosure (CVSS 9.8)
records.headline: Cisco's mail gateway can be rooted by one crafted email; found in a TAC support case, exploitation confirmed
records.summary: Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-76461 (CVSS 9.8) on 2026-09-14: an unauthenticated attacker who sends a single crafted email containing SQL statements to a Cisco Secure Email Gateway can execute arbitrary OS commands as root. Cisco confirms active exploitation and says the flaw was found during the resolution of a TAC support case; there is no workaround. CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day. Cisco simultaneously shipped a hardening release fixing five further internally-found vulnerabilities in the same product; Cisco's hardening advisory says two vulnerabilities from its internal review are known to be exploited, this one and the arbitrary file write CVE-2026-76519. On 2026-10-31 Cisco re-released the 15.5.5-014 fix in light of new information related to exploit code available online, so a 15.5 appliance patched earlier needs a check of its Retro Remediation Engine version. Public Metasploit modules now exist for the exploited injection (merged 2026-11-05, its author's medium-confidence match to CVE-2026-76461) and for a second S/MIME injection that its author believes is CVE-2026-76443, for which Cisco names no fixed 16.0 build.
actions: Upgrade every Cisco Secure Email Gateway appliance (physical and virtual) to AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 as re-released on 2026-10-31 (on an appliance that took the earlier build, confirm with retroscannerstatus that Retro Remediation Engine runs 4.0.2 or later), 16.0.4-302, or 16.5.0-780 (Cisco's recommended target) now; 16.0.4-302 closes CVE-2026-76461 only, because the hardening advisory names no fixed 16.0 release, so move a 16.0 appliance to 16.5.0-780 to close the five hardening-release CVEs (CVE-2026-76440, CVE-2026-76441, CVE-2026-20353, CVE-2026-76443, CVE-2026-76442) as well, one of which, CVE-2026-76443, has a public Metasploit module according to its author.

Grep every appliance's mail_logs (and, if clustered, every cluster member's logs) for the pattern "COPY.*TO PROGRAM" and cross-check firewall/network logs external to the appliance for unexpected outbound connections; a successful exploit grants root, so an attacker may have removed local log evidence of their own access; a clean result does not rule out the S/MIME injection, which did not leave that pattern in the module author's reproduction.

Secure Email Cloud customers should confirm directly with Cisco whether their instance is among those where indicators of compromise were identified; Cisco states it has already proactively contacted affected Cloud customers and upgraded all Cloud instances.

last_update.summary: Siemens revised its advisory SSA-834709 to V1.1 on 2026-11-04 and now lists the SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced, Basic, M.2 and SM variants as affected, all versions below V4.3.4-1 with Node-RED installed; the fix and interim mitigations are unchanged, so owners of the three further variants are in scope as well.

last_development.summary: Siemens revised its advisory SSA-834709 to V1.1 on 2026-11-04 and now lists the SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced, Basic, M.2 and SM variants as affected, all versions below V4.3.4-1 with Node-RED installed; the fix and interim mitigations are unchanged, so owners of the three further variants are in scope as well.

records.title: CVE-2026-58115, Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced, Basic, M.2 and SM ship a Node-RED interface with no authentication, so one unauthenticated HTTP request runs code with maximum privileges on an OT edge gateway (CVSS 10.0); VulnCheck's canary caught exploitation
records.headline: VulnCheck caught exploitation of the Node-RED flaw in Siemens IoT2050; all four variants affected, V4.3.4-1 fixes
records.summary: Siemens ProductCERT advisory SSA-834709 of 2026-08-11 discloses CVE-2026-58115, rated 10.0 on both CVSS 3.1 and 4.0: SIMATIC IoT2050 devices running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed do not enforce authentication on the Node-RED HTTP interface, so an unauthenticated attacker with network reach can create a flow and run code with maximum privileges. Siemens' advisory, revised on 2026-11-04, lists the Advanced, Basic, M.2 and SM variants, all versions below V4.3.4-1; V4.3.4-1 is the fix, and Siemens offers uninstalling or hardening Node-RED as interim mitigations. VulnCheck reports that on 2026-10-30 one of its canaries caught exploitation, a single request that deployed a flow downloading and running a Linux bot, with web-shell flows from the same address since; the target was a canary and the activity looks like opportunistic mass scanning.
actions: Update every SIMATIC IoT2050 (Advanced, Basic, M.2 and SM) to V4.3.4-1 or later now; where that cannot happen at once, uninstall Node-RED on units that do not use it, since Siemens names uninstalling or hardening Node-RED as its interim mitigations and exploitation takes a single unauthenticated request.

On every Node-RED instance that was reachable from an untrusted network, review the deployed flows for exec nodes and http-in endpoints that nobody built, and the access logs for POST requests to /flows from non-engineering addresses.

records.title: Seqrite: reverse engineering of two Qilin builds shows the October 2026 variant adding a vCenter and ESXi spreading engine, Restart Manager lock release, a Safe Mode reboot loop and ransom notes printed to office printers
records.headline: Qilin's October build spreads through vCenter and ESXi, reboots into Safe Mode and prints notes on office printers
records.summary: Seqrite compares a March 2026 and an October 2026 Qilin (Agenda) sample and reports that the newer build embeds a PowerShell engine that logs in to vCenter, disables HA and DRS and pushes Linux payloads to ESXi hosts over SSH, shuts down the processes that lock files through the Windows Restart Manager instead of brute-force termination, sets a Safe Mode reboot so EDR drivers do not load, and sends ransom notes to TCP 9100 on local subnets. It is a vendor analysis of two samples with no incident confirmation.

records.title: Microsoft Email Threat Landscape Q3 2026: tenant and user overrides delivered spoofed business-service mail that failed authentication, SVG attachments return as CAPTCHA-phishing carriers, and Teams impersonators move to ordinary personal names
records.headline: Microsoft Q3 email report: overrides let authentication-failing spoofed mail through; SVG CAPTCHA phishing returns
records.summary: Microsoft's Q3 2026 email-threat report finds that many malicious messages spoofing the sender domains of business services were delivered despite failing authentication because tenant- or user-level overrides applied, 63% of the messages with a recorded security outcome in September. It also reports SVG attachments leading CAPTCHA-gated phishing at quarter end, Teams impersonators shifting from help-desk display names to ordinary personal names, and an August device-code phishing campaign that used a QR code in a Word document against legal organisations.

records.title: Kaspersky reconstructs an intrusion through SharePoint ToolShell, attributed to Storm-2603 with moderate confidence, whose implant lived only inside w3wp.exe: an ASP.NET VirtualPathProvider memory shell with a suo5 tunnel, then Velociraptor, several tunnelling mechanisms and Warlock's AV killer
records.headline: Storm-2603-linked SharePoint intrusion: memory-only VirtualPathProvider shell in w3wp.exe, then Velociraptor and tunnels
records.summary: Kaspersky's retrospective of a December intrusion at a customer's on-premises SharePoint server, which it attributes to Storm-2603 with moderate confidence, shows a ToolShell exploit that left no file on disk: a C# memory shell registered as an ASP.NET VirtualPathProvider inside the IIS worker process w3wp.exe, dormant until a specific User-Agent arrived, with an suo5 proxy that turned the SharePoint host into a pivot. The actor then installed an outdated Velociraptor and several tunnelling mechanisms so access outlived the worker process, and Kaspersky's endpoint product blocked the Warlock encryption attempt.

records.title: CVE-2026-109593 and CVE-2026-109594, SonicWall GMS 9.5.2 and earlier: an unauthenticated network attacker may read internal GMS files (CVSS 3.1 9.1), and SonicWall says the end-of-life product gets no fix and has no workaround
records.headline: SonicWall GMS 9.5.2 and earlier: unauthenticated file read, no fix will ship; replace with NSM
records.summary: SonicWall's advisory SNWLID-2026-0019 of 2026-11-03 says an unauthenticated attacker with network access to SonicWall GMS 9.5.2 and earlier may read internal GMS files (CVE-2026-109593, CVSS 3.1 9.1), with a post-authentication SQL injection beside it (CVE-2026-109594, 6.8). The product reached end of support on 2026-09-30, so SonicWall releases no fix, names no workaround and urges migration to Network Security Manager; the advisory says nothing about exploitation.
actions: Find every SonicWall GMS instance on 9.5.2 or earlier, Virtual Appliance or Windows, cut its reachability from untrusted networks and schedule its replacement with Network Security Manager, because SonicWall will release no fix and names no workaround.

records.title: Sekoia: an APT29-linked watering hole serves n-day iOS and Android exploit chains through compromised sites, clone domains and a one-week compromise of the Plerdy tracker; CISA lists the Apple WebKit pointer-authentication bypass CVE-2024-27834 as exploited on 2026-11-04
records.headline: APT29-linked watering hole uses n-day iOS and Chrome chains; CISA lists CVE-2024-27834; updated devices resist
records.summary: Sekoia reports a watering-hole campaign it assesses with moderate to high confidence to be APT29 or a subgroup, serving platform-specific exploit chains for iOS 16.7, a DarkSword-based iOS chain and Chrome 139 to 145 on Android through injected sites, clone domains and a one-week compromise of the Plerdy analytics script; Sekoia says none of the chains works against fully updated devices. CISA added the Apple WebKit pointer-authentication bypass CVE-2024-27834, the second step of the iOS 16.7 chain and fixed in May 2024, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-04; no Swiss victim is named.
actions: Move every managed iPhone and iPad to the newest iOS available for its model and every managed Android phone to Chrome 146 or later and the OEM patch level that fixes CVE-2025-27038, and list the devices that cannot go past iOS 16.7.x (iPhone 8, 8 Plus, X, iPad 5th generation, iPad Pro 9.7-inch and 12.9-inch 1st generation per Apple), because Sekoia's chains do not work against fully updated devices and CISA lists all eight flaws they deliver as exploited.

records.title: CVE-2026-114424 and CVE-2026-114425, SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.1: an unauthenticated mail sender can reach root command execution through a replacement rule and root file access through Large File Transfer, with three more flaws fixed in the same release and no fix for the 15.0 branch (CVSS 4.0 9.2)
records.headline: SEPPmail gateway: unauthenticated sender reaches root RCE or file access; fixed in 15.1.1, 15.0.x has no fix
records.summary: SEPPmail's patch release 15.1.1 of 2026-11-03 fixes five flaws in the Secure Email Gateway, with NCSC.ch as the CNA: CVE-2026-114424 lets an unauthenticated remote sender run operating-system commands as root through an active address-replacement rule that uses message-derived data, and CVE-2026-114425 lets one disclose, move or delete files as root when Large File Transfer is enabled (both CVSS 4.0 9.2). The vendor says 15.0.7 was the last 15.0 release, so 15.0.x gateways must move to the 15.1 branch; no source reports exploitation.
actions: Upgrade every SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway to 15.1.1 now, moving 15.0.x gateways to the 15.1 branch because 15.0.7 is the last 15.0 release, and check each gateway's active address-replacement rules for values taken from the message and its Large File Transfer setting, the two conditions the CNA names.

records.title: SpecterOps: a Windows iSCSI Target Server set up without CHAP lets any host that knows the target and an authorised initiator name read the shared disks below file permissions, a Hyper-V domain controller's among them
records.headline: SpecterOps: iSCSI Target Server without CHAP lets a host that knows the target and initiator names read shared disks
records.summary: SpecterOps (2026-11-04) shows that a Windows iSCSI Target Server configured as a common cluster guide describes, with the optional CHAP step skipped, accepts a login from any host that knows the target host, the target name and an authorised initiator name, and the post says the host and the names can be found. The attacker then reads the shared disk below file-system permissions; where it holds a Hyper-V domain controller's virtual disk, the directory database and local credential stores are exposed. CHAP, network segmentation and volume encryption are the levers.
actions: List the computers in Active Directory that carry the service principal name the iSCSI Target Server registers and every host that listens on TCP 3260, then enable CHAP on each target and restrict TCP 3260 to the addresses of the cluster nodes, starting with targets whose volumes hold Hyper-V disks of domain controllers.

records.title: Canton Vaud warns of a device-code phishing campaign against Microsoft 365 accounts running in French-speaking Switzerland, with several organisations already affected
records.headline: Vaud: device-code phishing against Microsoft 365 is running in Romandie; several organisations already affected
records.summary: The canton of Vaud said on 2026-11-04 that a Microsoft 365 device-code phishing campaign is running in French-speaking Switzerland and that several organisations are already affected: mail that appears to come from a company or a known contact leads the reader to type a code on a genuine Microsoft sign-in page, which gives the attacker access to the account. Microsoft documents a Conditional Access policy that blocks the device code flow for tenants that do not need it.
actions: In every Microsoft 365 tenant your organisation runs or administers, audit device code sign-ins with the authentication protocol filter of the sign-in logs and, where no documented device needs the flow, create a Conditional Access policy with the Authentication flows condition set to Device code flow and Block access, starting in report-only mode and excluding emergency-access accounts and, where devices register through it, the Device Registration Service.

records.title: 3AM ransomware affiliate in a UK school estate: Bitdefender documents backup-credential theft, rogue domain admins and new two-way trusts between Active Directory domains, with a command-retry pattern it reads as a model-driven loop
records.headline: Bitdefender: a 3AM affiliate joined a school estate's AD domains with new trusts after stealing Veeam credentials
records.summary: Bitdefender MDR describes a September 2026 intrusion by a 3AM ransomware affiliate into a UK school estate that began as several unconnected Active Directory domains: a modified public Veeam script decrypted credentials stored on three backup servers, the attacker created two backdoor domain-administrator accounts, joined three domains with new two-way trusts within about three hours, tried to remove EDR agents (anti-tampering blocked it) and encrypted machines. Initial access is unknown, every attacker action Bitdefender saw came from an unmanaged internal host, and Bitdefender reads the 40 to 101 second retry cadence as a model-driven loop, flagged as its own interpretation; it says a new trust between domains is a rare change that is cheap to alert on.

last_update.summary: Sourcing note now records that the vendor's earlier advisory, repeated by BleepingComputer, described stolen CDN credentials as the access path, which its later disclosure replaced.

records.title: OPSSHIELD cPGuard: an attacker who registered as a customer reached the vendor's billing and licensing server and shipped a fake update on 2026-11-02 that ran as root on about 2,950 Linux servers, copying root secrets and leaving a root shell and a scheduled task
records.headline: cPGuard update channel pushed a fake root update to about 2,950 servers on 2 Nov; update, then rotate root secrets
records.summary: OPSSHIELD's disclosure of 2026-11-03 says an attacker registered as a customer on its billing portal and ran commands on the billing and licensing server, through crafted requests to the portal's callback pages (the vendor's logs do not record the exact request that gave access), took the keys used to publish updates and shipped a fake cPGuard update for about 70 minutes on 2026-11-02 (02:08 to 03:20 UTC). The update ran as root on about 2,950 customer servers, copied password hashes, root SSH keys, the MySQL root password and root shell history (cloud storage keys on a few) and left a hidden root shell and a scheduled task; about 7,900 billing-portal accounts were exposed as well. The clean update 5.88.26 removes the shell and a follow-up update removes the task, but credentials copied before cleanup may still be usable.
actions: On every Linux server that ran cPGuard on 2026-11-02, update to the latest version (the disclosure names 5.88.26 as the clean update), confirm that the hidden root shell and the scheduled task the fake update left are gone, then reset root and local passwords from a trusted environment and rotate the root SSH keys, the MySQL root password, any cloud storage keys and every secret in root's shell history; rebuild from a clean backup taken before 1 November any server the vendor tells you the attacker logged in to by hand.

last_update.summary: Priority re-graded from critical to high: the full-chain fix has been out since 2026-10-29 and the in-window items since then are confirmations of known exploitation, not new exploitation or weaponisation; the upgrade and compromise check stay in the entry's actions.

last_development.summary: Ivanti patched the root-escalation step of the exploited Connect Secure chain, CVE-2026-111357, on 2026-10-29, and CISA listed it and a third chain flaw, CVE-2026-118527, on 2026-10-30. The Canadian Cyber Centre and CISA now list builds 25.1.1.2 and 22.8R2.5 as affected, so the builds of 2026-10-13 are no longer the target.

records.title: CVE-2026-104935, Ivanti Connect Secure: an authentication bypass chained to code execution is exploited as a zero-day, the root-escalation step was patched on 2026-10-29 and CISA lists all three chain flaws (CVSS 8.6)
records.headline: Ivanti Connect Secure chain: root step patched 29 Oct, CISA lists three flaws; 25.1.1.2 and 22.8R2.5 fall short
records.summary: Ivanti disclosed the exploited Connect Secure authentication bypass CVE-2026-104935 on 2026-10-13; Volexity saw it chained by UTA0576 with a root escalation, CVE-2026-111357, patching library code in memory only so Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool sees no file change, and going after the appliance's Active Directory service account, LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys. Ivanti patched the root step on 2026-10-29 and CISA listed it and a third chain flaw, CVE-2026-118527, on 2026-10-30; the Canadian Cyber Centre now lists every build before 25.1.1.3, 25.1.3.1 and 22.8R2.6 as affected, which takes in 25.1.1.2 and 22.8R2.5, the builds of 2026-10-13. A patched appliance that was exposed still needs a compromise check, and CERT-FR says it knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance and tells owners to isolate and preserve it before any reset.
actions: Upgrade every Ivanti Connect Secure appliance to 25.1.1.3, 25.1.3.1 or 22.8R2.6 now, internet-facing appliances first: the Canadian Cyber Centre lists every earlier build as affected, so appliances that took only the 2026-10-13 builds 25.1.1.2 or 22.8R2.5 are still short of the root-step patch; 22.7.x and below are not affected.

Run a compromise check on every appliance that was reachable on an affected build, starting with proxy, load balancer or WAF logs back to at least 2026-10-03 for welcome.cgi requests that carry an X-DSCGI-PATH header; where compromise cannot be excluded, first cut the appliance off from the internet and the internal network and snapshot a virtual appliance's file system and memory without powering it down, then follow Ivanti's recovery steps and reset the domain service account, LAPS and local passwords, certificates, API keys, the Kerberos tickets of its service accounts and the licence-server authentication the appliance held, because CERT-FR knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets.

last_update.summary: Progress's bulletin carries fifteen WS_FTP Server flaws, six of them critical; CVE-2026-90868, CVE-2026-90866, CVE-2026-90864 and CVE-2026-90863 need privileges, and NCSC Switzerland describes four of the critical flaws as a route from the exposed administrator credentials to full server compromise.

records.title: CVE-2026-84295, Progress WS_FTP Server: an unauthenticated remote authentication flaw can expose administrative credentials (CVSS 10.0), with two more unauthenticated flaws, fixed in 2025.0.4 and 2024.0.7; no exploitation found
records.headline: WS_FTP Server: unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 admin-credential leak, five more critical flaws; fix 2025.0.4, 2024.0.7
records.summary: Progress's bulletin, as listed by heise, covers fifteen WS_FTP Server flaws on Windows, six of them critical: CVE-2026-84295, an improper-authentication flaw that could let an unauthenticated remote attacker reach administrative credentials (CVSS 3.1 10.0), and five command-injection, path-traversal and missing-authorization flaws (CVE-2026-90868 at 9.9, CVE-2026-90866, CVE-2026-90864 and CVE-2026-90863 at 9.1, CVE-2026-90865 at 9.0), four of which NCSC Switzerland describes as a route from the exposed administrator credentials to full server compromise. Builds before 2024.0.7 and 2025.0.4 are affected, and CSIRT Italia says Progress will issue no patch for unsupported versions. NCSC Switzerland lists exploitation as unknown and no source reports it; CISA's catalog holds no 2026 WS_FTP flaw, though a 2023 flaw in the same product is listed with known ransomware use.
actions: Upgrade every WS_FTP Server on Windows to 2024.0.7 or 2025.0.4 now, partner-facing and internet-reachable instances first, and rotate its administrator credentials afterwards, because CVE-2026-84295 can expose them to an unauthenticated attacker and the upgrade does not change what was already read; an instance on an unsupported branch gets no patch from Progress, so take it off the network or migrate it.

records.title: NIK C2: Talos documents a Go Windows implant that sends operator prompts to the OpenAI API from the infected host and falls back to the victim's own API key
records.headline: Talos: NIK C2 implant calls the OpenAI API from the victim host and bills the victim's own key if none is given
records.summary: Cisco Talos describes NIK C2, a command-and-control framework seen with a live server, whose Go implant for Windows has more than 52 commands and an ai_generate command that builds an OpenAI Chat Completions request on the infected host from an operator prompt. If the operator supplies no key the implant reads the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable, so OpenAI bills and logs the victim's key; Talos names no victims, sector or initial-access method.

records.title: Dahua cameras and recorders: CERT-UA warns that attackers take devices over through the Easy4IP cloud relay even when no port is exposed, then view video, change configuration and add accounts
records.headline: CERT-UA: Dahua cameras are taken over through the Easy4IP cloud even with no port exposed; turn P2P off
records.summary: Ukraine's CERT-UA reports, in an alert dated 2026-10-23, compromises of Dahua IP cameras and video recorders in which attackers viewed the stream, changed device settings and created accounts of their own. The main vector is Easy4IP, Dahua's peer-to-peer remote-access feature, which reaches a device through Dahua's cloud by its guessable serial number without any published port; passwords are then guessed or, CERT-UA says, the 2021 authentication-bypass flaws CVE-2021-33044 and CVE-2021-33045 are used on outdated firmware, a use eSecurity Planet says is unconfirmed in these cases.
actions: Turn off Easy4IP (P2P cloud access) on every Dahua camera and recorder that does not need it, and search each device's audit log for DVRIP logins from 127.0.0.1.

last_update.summary: The takeaway said CloudSOC SpanVA and CASMA have no fix; Broadcom's umbrella advisory lists none as of 2026-10-30, but their own advisories need a login, so the statement now says what the umbrella page shows.

records.title: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, Broadcom Symantec Endpoint Protection Manager, Carbon Black App Control Server, CloudSOC SpanVA and Content Analysis and Malware Analysis: PHP2Shell reaches the endpoint-security management servers; App Control Server 8.12.2 and 8.13.2 are the fixes Broadcom names
records.headline: PHP2Shell hits Broadcom endpoint-security servers: App Control 8.12.2 or 8.13.2; SEPM fix builds unconfirmed
records.summary: Broadcom's Enterprise Security Group advisory 39404, last revised on 2026-10-30, lists Carbon Black App Control Server, Symantec Endpoint Protection Manager (SEPM), the CloudSOC SpanVA Appliance and, since 2026-10-30, Content Analysis and Malware Analysis (CASMA) as affected by the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, and gives no versions, fixes or workarounds. Broadcom's article 459982 names App Control Server 8.12.2 and 8.13.2 as the fixes for all supported versions; the SEPM builds 14.3.27716.10000 and 14.4.494.0000 rest on a community report that NCSC-NL's tracker accepts, because Broadcom's SEPM advisory needs a login. CISA lists both PHP flaws as exploited, and Broadcom's advisory says nothing about attacks on these products.
actions: Install Carbon Black App Control Server 8.12.2 or 8.13.2 (8.13.2 where the server already runs 8.13), confirm the SEPM fix build against Broadcom's login-gated advisory 39421 before treating 14.3.27716.10000 or 14.4.494.0000 as the target, and until each server is fixed limit the management console of every SEPM, App Control Server, CloudSOC SpanVA appliance and CASMA to administrator networks.

last_update.summary: The sibling flaw CVE-2026-110264 reaches every GitLab version from 7.0, with backports to 19.1.9, 19.0.10 and 18.11.13, so instances older than 19.2 are in scope and have a fixed build; the Ruby project says any application that compiles attacker-controlled regular expressions is exposed until Ruby 4.0.9, 3.4.12 or 3.3.13.

last_development.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-97229 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-29 and NCSC Switzerland updated its advisory the same day to active exploitation, citing Alpine Linux's report that a newly registered account crashed its GitLab 19.3.4 workers eight times on 2026-10-20 and 21, after which Alpine rebuilt the instance. Alpine also found that GitLab's fix is a patch to the Ruby bundled in its own packages and images, so an installation with its own Ruby needs Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12 or 4.0.9 as well, and GitLab's builds of 2026-10-21 also fix a second CVSS 10 flaw, CVE-2026-110264. The CVE record moves to exploited and KEV-listed, the summary, detection, takeaway and action are rewritten, and the superseded status lines are removed.

records.title: CVE-2026-97229, GitLab CE/EE: an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular-expression compiler allows code execution on self-managed servers; exploited, fixed in 19.4.2, 19.3.5 and 19.2.8 (CVSS 10.0)
records.headline: GitLab's CVSS 10.0 CI regex RCE is now on CISA KEV; the public PoC needs push access to a public project
records.summary: GitLab's critical patch release of 2026-10-12 fixes CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS 3.1 10.0), an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular-expression compiler that lets code run on the server as the git user through a crafted expression in a CI/CD configuration. CISA listed it as exploited on 2026-10-29 and NCSC Switzerland reports active exploitation on the strength of Alpine Linux's account of a newly registered account that crashed its GitLab 19.3.4 workers eight times on 2026-10-20 and 21, after which Alpine rebuilt the instance because it could not rule out code execution; GitLab's fix is a patch to the Ruby bundled in its own packages and images, so an installation with its own Ruby needs Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12 or 4.0.9 as well. Self-managed CE and EE from 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5 and 19.4 before 19.4.2 are affected, Rapid7 published a proof of concept on 2026-10-13, and the path it demonstrated needs push access to a public project.
actions: Upgrade every self-managed GitLab CE and EE instance on 19.2, 19.3 or 19.4 to 19.2.8, 19.3.5 or 19.4.2 now, preferably to 19.2.9, 19.3.6, 19.4.3 or 19.5.1, which also fix CVE-2026-110264, internet-reachable instances and instances that allow open sign-up or public projects first, because CISA lists the flaw as exploited and NCSC Switzerland reports active exploitation; where GitLab runs on its own Ruby (a source install or a container image that does not use GitLab's packages) also install Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12 or 4.0.9, because the fix is a Ruby patch that only GitLab's official packages carry. On any instance that was reachable on an affected version, run the six detections GitLab published on its release page and treat the CI/CD variables, runner registration tokens and deploy keys of any hit, or of an instance where compromise cannot be ruled out, as exposed.

last_update.summary: Broadcom's revisions of 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-19 (the 8.0 U2f express patches and the 7.0 extended-support path) are now in the fixed builds and actions; the Infosecurity Magazine attribution and date are corrected, CISA's ransomware-use flag on CVE-2026-59310 is recorded, the network attack vector of the two lower-severity flaws and the researcher credit are fixed, and the headline is current.

last_development.summary: CISA added the ESX insufficient-logging flaw CVE-2026-41709 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28, and CrowdStrike says the actor WARP PANDA exploited it as a zero-day in vCenter-environment intrusions as late as early 2026; Broadcom's advisory still carries no exploitation statement. The CVE record moves to exploited and KEV-listed, and ESX audit logs can no longer be treated as a complete record of administrator activity.

records.title: VMSA-2026-0006, VMware vCenter: unauthenticated Directory Service auth bypass and Syslog traversal RCE (both CVSS 9.8), plus a VMXNET3 guest-to-host escape
records.headline: VMware vCenter's pre-auth Syslog RCE is exploited; patch it with the auth bypass and VMXNET3 escape, no workaround
records.summary: Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0006 (2026-07-29) fixes five flaws across VMware ESX, vCenter, Workstation and Fusion, and NCSC-CH, NCSC-NL and BSI CERT-Bund all carried it across 2026-07-28 and 2026-07-29. CVE-2026-59309 (CVSS 9.8) is an authentication bypass in vCenter's Directory Service reachable with nothing but network access to vCenter, and CVE-2026-59310 (CVSS 9.8) is a directory traversal in vCenter's Syslog server that reaches arbitrary code execution. CVE-2026-47876 (CVSS 9.3) is an out-of-bounds write in the VMXNET3 virtual network adapter that lets a guest administrator execute code on the ESX host, affecting only VMs using that adapter. No workaround exists for any of the five, so patching is the only control. All were reported privately to Broadcom, one of them through Pwn2Own, and CVE-2026-59310 has since been exploited in the wild and was added to CISA's KEV catalog on 2026-08-18; CISA also listed the ESX logging flaw CVE-2026-41709 as exploited on 2026-10-28, the day CrowdStrike said the actor WARP PANDA used it as a zero-day.
actions: Inventory which guest VMs use the VMXNET3 adapter and patch the ESX hosts carrying them to ESXi-9.1.0.0200, ESXi-9.0.2.0100, ESXi80U3k or ESXi80U2f: the escape is reachable from guest administrative privilege, which makes any tenant-operated or lower-trust VM on a shared host a path to the hypervisor.

Patch vCenter to 9.1.0.0300, 9.0.2.0100 or 8.0 U3k/U2f as applicable (vCenter 7.0 through Broadcom extended support), since there is no workaround, and on any appliance that was network-reachable and unpatched between 29 July and today, check the appliance's own scheduled-task and cron configuration for entries the platform team did not create, and its egress records for outbound SSH sessions from the appliance itself.

On the ESX hosts of any vCenter estate that was exposed or compromised, install the build that fixes CVE-2026-41709 and review administrator activity from vCenter task and event records and from syslog forwarded off the host, because Broadcom says the flaw lets an administrator act without being logged and CrowdStrike reports it used as a zero-day.

records.title: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, PHP (PHP2Shell): two unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in the runtime, fixed on 2026-10-21 in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, with attack traffic already observed and no upstream release for 8.1 and older (CVSS 4.0 9.2)
records.headline: PHP2Shell: CISA lists both flaws as exploited after honeypot code execution; update the runtime, not the CMS
records.summary: The PHP project released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 on 2026-10-21 to fix CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 4.0 9.2), two flaws in the runtime that allow unauthenticated remote code execution as the web worker account, most directly on Apache mod_php, with no upstream release for PHP 8.1 and older and a third path, CVE-2026-115560, left unfixed (keep session.upload_progress.enabled=0). CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26, after a honeypot operator documented 35 successful code executions on PHP 8.4.26 under single-worker mod_php and VulnCheck extended its working exploit across builds of PHP 8.2 to 8.5; GreyNoise's sensors have recorded shell sessions since 2026-10-28, Palo Alto Networks' advisory now reports active exploitation against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces, Dream Research recovered a custom build chained with the Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 that rooted 25 Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall and management servers and attacked a US government-affiliated network, SRF links a data theft at TCS Camping's booking-system supplier to the flaws without naming a CVE, and Unit 42 retracted on 2026-10-25 its update that linked an attack on a European government agency to them. As of 2026-10-22 BACS knew of no attack in Switzerland but said federal PHP applications were affected and that it had no complete overview of the update status, and Swiss cantons, universities, Cyon, the Lodur platform and Publica took sites offline as a precaution.
actions: Update the PHP runtime, not the CMS or its plugins, on every internet-facing server and container image to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 or to your distribution's patched package, restart PHP-FPM, Apache and every long-running worker, rebuild images, and confirm the running version, because a distribution backport can keep the old version string; isolate any application that cannot be updated from public networks until it is.

After updating, set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 on every PHP host and keep it there until PHP's next regular bugfix release: CVE-2026-115560, which the October releases do not fix, needs session upload progress to be enabled.

List every appliance and management server whose web interface embeds PHP (firewalls, network access control and security consoles), take each interface off the internet and install its vendor's PHP2Shell fix, because Dream Research reports Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewalls rooted through an exposed management interface.

records.title: CVE-2026-96951, Windows Shell: a Mark of the Web bypass exploited as a zero-day, fixed in the 2026-10-13 cumulative updates and listed in CISA KEV (CVSS 8.8)
records.headline: Microsoft patches an exploited Windows Shell zero-day that evades Mark of the Web protections on files and links
records.summary: Microsoft's 2026-10-13 updates fix CVE-2026-96951, a Windows Shell flaw that lets an attacker evade Mark of the Web defenses once a user opens a crafted file or link sent by email or instant message, so Windows does not show the dialog the tag normally triggers. Microsoft marks it exploited and CISA added it to KEV the same day; no source names the actor, the payload or the victims. Rapid7 says Windows Server 2012 gets no patch, while Microsoft lists fixes for Server 2012 R2 and every later supported release.
actions: Deploy the 2026-10-13 cumulative update for each release (KB5127648 for Windows 11 24H2, 25H2 and 26H2, KB5127646 for Windows 11 26H1, KB5126657 for Windows 10 21H2 and 22H2, KB5126655 for Server 2022, KB5126646 for Server 2025, and the others listed in the CVE record) to every Windows endpoint and server, starting with the systems whose users open mail and chat attachments or download files; Rapid7 says Windows Server 2012 receives no patch; confirm that Microsoft Edge is at 154.0.4258.62 or later, which Microsoft added to the fix list on 2026-10-26.

records.headline: Bern's cantonal cybersecurity law is in force: 24h/72h incident reporting and a named accountable officer per agency
records.summary: Canton Bern's government council confirmed on 2026-09-10 that its new Gesetz über Informations- und Cybersicherheit (ICSG) and implementing ordinance (IDSV) enter into force on 1 November 2026. From that date, every cantonal administrative unit must report cyberattacks and security incidents within 24 hours (72 hours where personal data is affected), classify ICT assets by protection need, and name each agency's top leadership as the accountable security officer. The baseline directive Grundschutz BE is expected in the first quarter of 2027, and its general terms on information security and data protection (AGB ISDS BE) must be agreed in cantonal contracts that cover processing information or personal data.

records.headline: GhostAction: fake security workflows now harvest whole git histories; rotating Actions secrets is not enough
records.summary: StepSecurity and Socket report that on 2026-10-08 the GhostAction campaign used the GitHub credentials of two open-source maintainers to commit a workflow disguised as a security audit straight to the default branch of 345 to 346 repositories, including one of an Uber-owned organisation, and that the workflow now sends the credentials found in the working tree and in the entire git history, besides the named Actions secrets, to a hardcoded address over plain HTTP. GitGuardian's own data puts the wave of 8 to 12 October at more than 30,000 repositories reached through about 1,900 compromised GitHub accounts, and says GitHub has prevented the workflow from running since 9 October. Between 13 and 21 October the operator pushed at least 72,026 further commits, mostly from accounts whose tokens were already used on 8 October, including a stealer disguised as a font file that a hidden VS Code task runs on developer machines, outside GitHub's workflow hold, and a cron job that survives cleaning the repository.
actions: Run an organisation-scoped GitHub code search in every organisation your teams and suppliers administer for workflow files under .github/workflows that present themselves as a security audit, a security check or an Actions security workflow and were added since 2026-08-31; any hit means assume breach: revoke the credential that committed it, rotate every secret found anywhere in the repository's git history, not only the configured Actions secrets, and check the crontab of every developer machine and self-hosted runner that opened or ran the repository since 2026-10-14 for a five-minute job that runs a remote script.

records.summary: Microsoft released .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14 and 11 Release Candidate 3 out of band on 2026-10-25 to fix the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497 (CVSS 3.1 8.1, publicly disclosed, rated Exploitation More Likely) and to deliver the corrected fixes for CVE-2026-70197 (Windows sockets memory corruption, CVSS 3.1 8.1) and CVE-2026-102870 (Blazor debugger), which the 2026-10-13 release did not fully address. records.title: CVE-2026-46300, Linux kernel: local privilege escalation via xfrm ESP-in-TCP ("Fragnesia"), listed by CISA as exploited and chained with the PHP2Shell flaws to reach root, PoC public
records.headline: CVE-2026-46300 (Fragnesia): CISA lists the Linux kernel root flaw as exploited, chained with PHP2Shell
records.summary: CVE-2026-46300 ("Fragnesia", CVSS 7.8) is a local privilege escalation in the Linux kernel's xfrm ESP-in-TCP path, one of three CVEs Red Hat groups as "Dirty Frag"; CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28 and says it can be chained with the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root, and Dream Research reports such a chain against 25 Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall and management servers and a US government-affiliated network. Its public exploit overwrites /usr/bin/su in the page cache, and Red Hat confirms RHEL kernels are affected (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28 · Dream Research, 2026-10-29 · Red Hat RHSB-2026-003).
actions: Patch CVE-2026-46300 on every Linux host that runs PHP or other internet-facing code, then on multi-tenant hosts, container nodes and CI runners: apply the distribution kernel update and reboot; until then, where IPsec is not in use, block and unload the `esp4`, `esp6` and `rxrpc` modules (this breaks IPsec), and drop the page cache so a file already modified in memory reloads from disk.

On any PHP web host, appliance or management server that was reachable and unpatched for the PHP2Shell flaws, look for PHP files in web-reachable directories that nobody deployed, an outbound SSH session from the host that a systemd service or an rc.local entry keeps up, and password-spray bursts against Active Directory from the host's address, because Dream Research reports a chain of the two flaws that did exactly that.

records.title: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS and Panorama: the PHP2Shell flaws affect every release below its train's hotfix through the management web interface, and Palo Alto reports active exploitation against internet-exposed management interfaces; all twenty hotfixes are out
records.headline: PAN-OS management interfaces were rooted in the wild via PHP2Shell and a kernel flaw: hotfix, then check for compromise
records.summary: Palo Alto Networks' advisory, first published on 2026-10-21 and revised since, says active exploitation has been observed against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet, and Dream Research, with Unit 42's verification, reports a custom PHP2Shell build chained with a Linux kernel flaw that rooted 25 PAN-OS firewall and management servers in the United States, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea and went on to attack a US government-affiliated Active Directory. The advisory lists every release below the hotfix for its train, of PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1, 11.2, 11.1 and 10.2 and of Panorama, as affected through the management web interface by CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS-B 9.2); all twenty hotfixes are released, and GlobalProtect and the captive portal are not affected. A device that was exposed and unpatched needs a compromise check as well as the hotfix, and CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26.
actions: Take the management interface of every PA-Series and VM-Series firewall and Panorama off the internet now by restricting it to a jump box or trusted internal addresses, because Palo Alto reports active exploitation against internet-exposed management interfaces, and install the hotfix for your maintenance release, which Palo Alto's table lists for every line from 10.2.7 to 12.2.4 (11.2.10-h17 adds the Brotli fix).

Rotate the directory bind account, HA replication keys, certificate private keys and device authentication keys of every PAN-OS firewall and Panorama that was reachable from the internet while unpatched and shows a PHP web shell or a tunnel, because the chain Dream Research recovered harvested exactly those from rooted firewalls, and the hotfix does not remove a web shell or tunnel already in place.

records.title: Teams help-desk impersonation to domain-controller identity: Microsoft traces two intrusions from a Quick Assist session to AD CS ESC1 certificates with DCSync, and to PetitPotam relayed to ESC8 Web Enrollment
records.headline: Microsoft: Teams help-desk vishing into Quick Assist ended in AD CS certificates for privileged accounts and a DC
records.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes two human-operated intrusions, not attributed to any actor, in which an external Teams contact impersonating help-desk staff got a user to open Quick Assist, after which the operator staged a portable runtime and used Active Directory Certificate Services to reach privileged identities: a template open to ESC1 issued certificates for privileged accounts and DCSync followed within seconds, and in the second case PetitPotam was relayed to AD CS Web Enrollment (ESC8) for a certificate for a domain controller account. An issued certificate stays valid after a password reset or a reimage of the first workstation, and in the first case one privileged account excluded from automated containment stayed usable and was used to copy data to an external SFTP destination.
actions: In every forest with an enterprise CA, list the AD CS Web Enrollment and Certificate Enrollment Web Service endpoints that lack HTTPS and Extended Protection for Authentication and the certificate templates that accept requester-supplied identity with broad enrollment rights, because both intrusions turned a Quick Assist session into a certificate for a privileged identity.

records.title: Cursor marketplace: a tampered Claude Code extension (versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313) planted an SSH key, a reverse tunnel and persistence for about eleven hours on 2026-10-29; uninstalling it does not remove the persistence
records.headline: Cursor marketplace served a trojanised Claude Code extension for 11 hours; uninstalling leaves the SSH backdoor
records.summary: Between about 09:27 and 20:35 UTC on 2026-10-29 the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace served a modified copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for macOS and Windows, that appends an attacker's SSH key to authorized_keys, tries to enable SSH and open a reverse tunnel, and installs persistence that outlives the extension. Coding errors made the SSH step fail on most standard-user hosts, so Cursor and Sophos say the attacker could not log in there, but the key, the persistence and a host report were still written. Anthropic told Microsoft its systems were not compromised, and no source says how the attacker published under Anthropic's name.
actions: On every developer endpoint that runs Cursor, check extension-install telemetry for Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 installed between 09:27 and 20:35 UTC on 2026-10-29; where it is found, isolate the host, remove the unauthorized SSH key, the persistence and any running tunnel process, because uninstalling the extension removes none of them, and rotate every credential reachable from the host from a trusted system.

records.headline: Drupal Commerce Core access bypass is exploited in the wild; update to 3.3.13 or 8.x-2.41 and audit orders
records.summary: Drupal's advisory SA-CONTRIB-2026-254 of 2026-10-28 says an access bypass in the Commerce Core module, which adds a shopping cart and checkout to Drupal sites, is being actively exploited in the wild; the Drupal security team scores it 21 of 25, needing no authentication and affecting every module configuration. Commerce Core 3.0.0 up to but not including 3.3.13, and earlier releases before 8.x-2.41, are affected, and Drupal tells operators to update and audit their orders for inconsistencies. NCSC Switzerland issued its own advisory on 2026-10-30; Drupal says nothing on the method, the actor or the number of sites hit.
actions: Update Commerce Core on every Drupal site to 3.3.13 (3.x) or 8.x-2.41 (earlier releases) now, then audit orders back as far as your logs reach for inconsistencies, because Drupal says the flaw is exploited, names no other mitigation and does not say when exploitation began.

records.title: CVE-2026-102764, BeyondTrust Remote Support: an unauthenticated file-operation flaw exploited as a zero-day since late August by a suspected China-nexus actor that left a web shell and boot-time sudo persistence (CVSS 4.0 9.3)
records.headline: BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day: Rapid7 reports a Metasploit module; the actor's persistence survives reset
records.summary: BeyondTrust's advisory BT26-05 of 2026-10-15 fixes CVE-2026-102764, an improper origin validation in an internal messaging component of Remote Support that lets a remote attacker perform file operations on the appliance without authenticating; all versions up to 26.2.3 are affected. Google's Threat Intelligence Group found ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor formerly tracked as UNC5221, exploiting it as a zero-day in late August 2026, leaving a web shell, a root-SUID shell and a sudoers entry that survive reboot and configuration reset, so a patched appliance that was exposed still needs a compromise check, and a rebuild where its status is confirmed or unknown. Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis on 2026-10-30, and a Metasploit module now implements the chain.
actions: Apply the BT26-05-RS patch to every self-hosted BeyondTrust Remote Support appliance now and confirm in the /appliance interface that it is installed (a build older than 24.3.1 must be upgraded first, which closes the hole but does not undo earlier exposure); apply it to self-hosted Privileged Remote Access appliances too, since BeyondTrust built and tested the patch for both products although its advisory names only Remote Support as impacted.

For every appliance that was internet-reachable on a build up to 26.2.3 at any time since late August 2026: before any change, snapshot a virtual appliance with memory and export its disk, and collect the off-box syslog, reverse-proxy or WAF and perimeter firewall logs because the actor deletes on-appliance logs; then redeploy from a clean, fully patched image every appliance whose compromise status is confirmed or unknown, and rotate the credentials it held in dependency order, including the Remote Support Vault and any credential typed into a support session.

records.headline: Lumen: Volt Typhoon's Silent Train relay chains fronted zero-days against SD-WAN, N-central and KACE
records.summary: Lumen's Black Lotus Labs reports that Volt Typhoon ran exploitation, credential access and exfiltration through Silent Train, rotating chains of compromised SOHO, IoT and enterprise devices that it rebuilt for each operation, and that its monitoring uncovered one likely and four confirmed zero-day campaigns against endpoint and network management platforms and SD-WAN orchestrators, among them Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, N-able N-central and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator. The reported victims are US-centred and the report names no Swiss or European victim.

records.title: VAPOR PANDA: CrowdStrike reports a China-nexus actor running the ARTEX agent framework against more than 200 organisations from 17 October, among them foreign ministries in Europe and a Greek government entity, and deploying the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor
records.headline: CrowdStrike: VAPOR PANDA runs ARTEX against 200+ organisations, European foreign ministries among them
records.summary: CrowdStrike reports that from 2026-10-17 the China-nexus actor VAPOR PANDA used the ARTEX agent framework, driven mainly by the DeepSeek model, against more than 200 organisations worldwide, with the controller CrowdStrike saw directing exploitation in at least 14 countries, including foreign ministries in Europe, a European country's presidency, prime minister's office and defence, justice, finance and intelligence entities, and a Greek government entity. CrowdStrike confirmed post-exploitation at nine organisations, with the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor loaded by a renamed legitimate binary, and says this campaign is separate from the Storm-0940 ARTEX activity Microsoft reported.

records.title: ANNUAL REPORT: Cisco Talos Incident Response trends Q3 2026: public administration tied with finance as the most targeted sector, help-desk vishing into remote-management tools, and ransomware operators uninstalling and killing EDR
records.headline: Talos IR Q3: public administration tied for most targeted; vishing into RMM and EDR killing mark the ransomware cases
records.summary: Cisco Talos Incident Response's Q3 2026 trends report names public administration, tied with finance at 18 percent of engagements, as the most targeted sector, and puts phishing first and public-facing application exploitation second among initial-access techniques. Its ransomware cases (27 percent of engagements) show help-desk vishing that leads the victim to allow remote access through a legitimate remote-management tool, and operators who uninstall or terminate EDR, including with vulnerable drivers.

records.title: CVE-2026-76418, Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and Secure FTD: a crafted request to the remote access SSL VPN reloads the device when a tunnel group uses secondary authentication; Cisco reports active exploitation and CISA lists it (CVSS 3.1 8.6)
records.headline: Cisco ASA and FTD SSL VPN reload flaw is exploited and on CISA KEV; fixes in every branch, no workaround
records.summary: Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-28 fixes CVE-2026-76418, a logic error in the remote access SSL VPN of Secure Firewall ASA and Secure FTD that lets an unauthenticated attacker reload the device with a crafted connection request when a tunnel group uses secondary authentication, and says Cisco's PSIRT became aware of active exploitation in October 2026; CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-29. Cisco names no actor, offers no workaround and lists first fixed releases for every ASA and FTD branch.
actions: Upgrade every Cisco ASA and FTD unit that has webvpn enabled and secondary authentication on any tunnel group, DefaultWEBVPNGroup included, to the first fixed release of its branch (ASA 9.16.4.104, 9.18.4.96, 9.20.4.50, 9.22.3.200, 9.23.1.48, 9.24.1.27 or 9.24.10.1; FTD 7.0.11, 7.2.13, 7.4.9, 7.6.7, 7.7.14, 10.0.3 or 10.1.1), internet-facing units first, because Cisco reports exploitation and its only mitigation removes secondary authentication.
