records.title: Linux kernel ZDI-CAN-33367: a public local root exploit for an skb_zerocopy page-cache write that gets past the Dirty Frag fix, with no CVE and no mainline fix, among six reports Trend Micro's ZDI copied to public lists, two of them ksmbd flaws scored CVSS 9.0
records.headline: Public root exploit for a Linux page-cache write past the Dirty Frag fix; AlmaLinux kernels carry the fix, no CVE yet
records.summary: Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative copied public Linux kernel lists on five kernel reports on 2026-10-21 before any fix was merged, and Sysdig ranks ZDI-CAN-33367 as the one to act on: a local privilege escalation through skb_zerocopy() that gets past the Dirty Frag fix, with a public exploit that TuxCare reproduced as root on AlmaLinux 8 to 10, CloudLinux 9 and 10, Debian 12 and 13 and Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04. A reviewed patch is in the kernel's networking tree but not in mainline, AlmaLinux announced on 2026-10-28 that fixed kernels are in production for 8, 9 and 10, none of the six reports has a CVE, and two ksmbd reports that ZDI scores CVSS 9.0 matter only where the in-kernel SMB server runs; no exploitation in the wild is reported.
actions: On every AlmaLinux host where untrusted users or workloads run code, install kernel-4.18.0-553.178.1.el8_10, kernel-5.14.0-687.60.1.el9_8 or kernel-6.12.0-211.69.1.el10_2 or later and reboot, or apply TuxCare's KernelCare patch on EL9 and EL10.

records.title: ConnectWise Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick): the vendor's Microsoft 365 application credential was used to sign in to customer tenants, with directory-role self-assignments in about 50 tenants and, Huntress reports, added credentials in two
records.headline: ConnectWise SkyKick app credential used in 162+ Microsoft 365 tenants; disabling it does not undo planted access
records.summary: ConnectWise says it identified unauthorized access to application identities of its Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) service; Huntress and Todyl report that from 15 October the app's credential was used to obtain app-only Microsoft Graph tokens in customer Microsoft 365 tenants; Huntress alone confirmed unauthorized sign-ins in 162 tenants by 16 October and saw ConnectWise Cloud Management apps assign themselves directory roles in about 50 tenants and, in two tenants, a scripted Global Administrator self-grant followed by new client secrets planted on apparently random applications. ConnectWise disabled seven application identities and suspended the service on 17 October, but says disabling does not reverse changes already made in a tenant, so every tenant that ever consented a ConnectWise or SkyKick app needs the apps disabled and its application credentials, directory roles and consents reviewed. Microsoft assesses that the China-state aligned actor Storm-0940 is behind it, using the ARTEX agentic-AI framework, and says it attempted sign-ins to more than 2,250 tenants; how the credential was obtained and what data was read are not public.
actions: In every Entra tenant you or your MSP administer, disable without deleting the seven ConnectWise application identities that ConnectWise lists by client ID (Cloud Backup is 506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae; the other six are in ConnectWise's advisory), dormant connections included, and keep them disabled, because ConnectWise's restoration of 2026-10-28 has partners consent a new application, “ConnectWise Cloud Backup for M365”, in each tenant, so take its details only from the instructions on ConnectWise's Trust Center; where Graph activity logs were enabled, review them for these apps until at least 90 minutes after you disabled them, because a token issued before the disable stays valid for up to 90 minutes, and preserve the sign-in and audit logs promptly without delaying containment, because Entra ID Free keeps only 7 days.
In the same tenants list the apps owned by the ConnectWise tenant (ID 3f9cd7a0-127a-4ed4-bf06-2f830d5616b7), and disable each that you do not use or cannot verify as safe.

In the same tenants review every enterprise application and app registration, MSP management and security tools first but none skipped (Huntress saw the secrets planted on apparently random applications, in one tenant on some of the least privileged ones), for client secrets, certificates and federated credentials added since 2026-10-13 and remove any you did not create; also check the directory roles, owners and consent grants held by ConnectWise and SkyKick service principals, Conditional Access exclusions for them, and mailbox forwarding, inbox and transport rules and delegated access, because disabling the vendor applications does not remove access planted through them.

records.title: Oracle October 2026 Critical Patch Update: six unauthenticated network CVSS 10.0 rows in Access Manager, SOA Suite, E-Business Suite and JD Edwards, and WebLogic CVSS 9.8 flaws reachable over HTTP and T3/IIOP
records.headline: Oracle's October CPU: six unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 rows, two WebLogic 9.8 flaws; EBS decoys probed on 27 Oct
records.summary: Oracle's Critical Patch Update of 2026-10-20 carries 1295 new patches. Its risk matrices list 90 rows (73 distinct CVE ids) scored CVSS 3.1 9.0 or higher that need no authentication over the network, among them six at 10.0 in Access Manager, SOA Suite (three), E-Business Suite Workflow Notification Mailer and JD Edwards EnterpriseOne Orchestrator, and two WebLogic Server flaws at 9.8 reachable over HTTP and over T3 and IIOP. The advisory states no exploitation for any row; Defused reported exploit attempts against its E-Business Suite decoys for CVE-2026-101767 on 2026-10-27, and no compromise of a production system is reported.
actions: Patch every E-Business Suite 12.2.3 to 12.2.15 web tier for CVE-2026-101767 now, because exploit attempts began a week after release, and review its web logs since 2026-10-27 for unauthenticated requests to the Thin Client Framework servlet and for database or Concurrent Manager activity that followed.

records.title: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, F5 BIG-IP: the PHP2Shell flaws reach the Configuration utility of every module and the APM and SSL Orchestrator access profiles on 17.1.0 to 17.1.3, 17.5.0 to 17.5.1 and 21.1.0, and F5's cumulative critical releases 17.1.3.7, 17.5.1.11 and 21.1.0.4 carry the fix
records.headline: F5 BIG-IP is affected by PHP2Shell: fixes are in 17.1.3.7, 17.5.1.11 and 21.1.0.4; APM data plane and TMUI exposed
records.summary: F5's release notes for BIG-IP 17.1.3.7, 17.5.1.11 and 21.1.0.4, each updated on 2026-10-24, list K000163821 as the fix for the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and call each a critical release whose only new changes are PHP fixes. NCSC-NL's record of K000163821 puts BIG-IP 17.1.0 to 17.1.3, 17.5.0 to 17.5.1 and 21.1.0 in scope, through the Configuration utility of all modules and through the access-profile data plane of APM and SSL Orchestrator; F5's article itself could not be read, and nothing found reports an attack on BIG-IP, although CISA lists both flaws as exploited.
actions: Update every F5 BIG-IP on 17.1, 17.5 or 21.1 to 17.1.3.7, 17.5.1.11 or 21.1.0.4, systems that publish an APM or SSL Orchestrator access profile first, because NCSC-NL records the access-profile data plane as exposed as well as the Configuration utility.

records.title: testmetest: an npm worm in the Miasma and Shai-Hulud family now starts when an application imports the package, so install with --ignore-scripts no longer protects, and JFrog finds 42 third-party GitHub repositories already armed with its publisher
records.headline: SafeDep and JFrog: the testmetest npm worm now runs on import, so --ignore-scripts does not stop it; 42 repos armed
records.summary: SafeDep and JFrog describe an npm worm, tracked as testmetest, whose newest builds start when an application imports the package, so installing with --ignore-scripts does not stop it. It steals SSH, registry, cloud, CI and AI-tool credentials, publishes new patch versions of the victim's own packages, and wipes the home directory when the stolen GitHub token is revoked. SafeDep counts 19 packages from one operator between 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-27; JFrog found 42 armed GitHub repositories of 11 legitimate owners; neither lab names an actor.
actions: Compare every lockfile and CI cache against the package list in SafeDep's post; on each host that installed or imported a listed package, disconnect it, remove persistence first and only then rotate the GitHub, npm, cloud and SSH credentials it could read, because the worm wipes the home directory when the stolen GitHub token is revoked.

records.title: MDaemon mail server below 26.0.4 and Windows ClamAV 0.101.0 to 1.5.3: a crafted RAR emailed to any address runs code on the server through the bundled UnRAR flaw CVE-2025-8088, and ESET saw Russia-aligned attackers use it in Ukraine to deploy the HELLAGE and HELLTAG backdoors
records.headline: ESET: an emailed RAR ran code on MDaemon servers via ClamAV's UnRAR; fixed in MDaemon 26.0.4, ClamAV 1.4.6 and 1.5.4
records.summary: ESET reports an active campaign in Ukraine in which Russia-aligned attackers exploited MDaemon mail servers: a crafted RAR archive mailed to any address makes MDaemon invoke ClamAV, whose old bundled UnRAR library carries the path-traversal flaw CVE-2025-8088, and the exploit writes a malicious DLL to the server with no user interaction. MDaemon fixed it in 26.0.4 on 2026-08-25, and ClamAV's own notes show that every Windows ClamAV from 0.101.0 to 1.5.3 is affected, fixed in 1.4.6 and 1.5.4. The attackers deployed the HELLAGE mail-stealing backdoor and the Telegram-controlled HELLTAG backdoor.
actions: Update every MDaemon mail server to 26.0.4 or later and every Windows host that scans mail or files with ClamAV to 1.4.6 or 1.5.4, then check each mail server for DLLs it should not hold and treat stored mail on a server that ran an older build as possibly read, because HELLAGE steals email.

records.title: Huntress: phished MDM enrolments in Hexnode and Rippling give attackers a management path that brings ScreenConnect back after it has been removed
records.headline: Huntress: phished MDM enrolments push ScreenConnect back after removal; the RMM is not the root of the intrusion
records.summary: Huntress reports several recent incidents in which phishing victims ended up with an MDM client from Hexnode or Rippling followed by an unauthorised ScreenConnect agent. In the Rippling case the attacker used the MDM, running with SYSTEM rights, to stage and run ScreenConnect; in the Hexnode case the managed-service provider removed ScreenConnect and it returned several hours later to the same relay while the Hexnode client was still installed. Huntress says the products are not at fault and that removing the RMM does not remove the management architecture behind it.
actions: On every endpoint from which an unauthorised ScreenConnect or other RMM agent has been removed, check for a Hexnode or Rippling MDM agent or enrolment that nobody authorised and unenrol the device from that tenant, because in Huntress's Hexnode case ScreenConnect returned hours after its removal while the MDM client stayed.

records.title: Machelen (Belgium) municipality: its own timeline shows a foothold through misleading instructions on an external website on 2026-08-20, found 22 days later after a high-privilege user was reached, with personal data confirmed stolen and Rhysida now listing municipal and social-welfare files
records.headline: Machelen municipality: foothold from a website's misleading instructions, 22 days to detection; Rhysida lists its files
records.summary: The Belgian municipality of Machelen published a timeline in which attackers gained access to an internal laptop through misleading instructions on an external website on 2026-08-20, reached a user with high privileges on 2026-09-10 and were found on 2026-09-11; it confirms that personal data was stolen. Ransomware.live recorded on 2026-10-27 that the Rhysida group had listed the municipal and social-welfare file servers on its leak site, a claim the municipality has not confirmed.

records.title: Moldova's government digital services: attackers used flaws in services reachable without authentication to query about one million national identification numbers and extract data on about 750,000 of them between 19 and 23 October, and the Prime Minister says AI allegedly helped find the flaws
records.headline: Moldova: unauthenticated e-government services queried for about one million ID numbers; data on 750,000 extracted
records.summary: Moldova's Electronic Governance Agency says that between 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-23 attackers exploited flaws in state digital services reachable without authentication to query about one million national identification numbers and, on preliminary estimates, extract data sets for about 750,000 of them, then used what they obtained to extract more from interconnected systems. The Prime Minister says foreign state involvement is being investigated and that AI allegedly helped find the flaws; Moldova has not attributed the attack, and the agency took 82 services under review and disconnected exposed services and more than 30 systems.

records.title: WatchGuard Fireware OS 2026.4, 12.12.4 and 12.5.22: seven of 17 fixed Fireware OS flaws are scored 9.0 or higher, among them unauthenticated memory-corruption and missing-authentication rows in the Access Portal, the SIP proxy and the FireCluster sync daemon; WatchGuard knows of no exploitation
records.headline: WatchGuard fixes three feature-dependent unauthenticated flaws scored 9.2 in Fireware OS; no exploitation known
records.summary: WatchGuard's advisories of 2026-10-27 fix 17 flaws in Fireware OS 2026.4, 12.12.4 and, for T15 and T35 models, 12.5.22, seven of them scored 9.0 or higher. Three need no authentication but a specific feature: a heap write in the Access Portal's WebSocket handling, a stack overflow in the SIP proxy and missing authentication in the FireCluster sync daemon, each scored 9.2. Four more need an attacker who controls or intercepts traffic to an Active Directory server, to WatchGuard Cloud or to a log server. WatchGuard is not aware of exploitation of any of them.
actions: Upgrade every WatchGuard Firebox to Fireware OS 2026.4, 12.12.4 or, on T15 and T35 models, 12.5.22, starting with appliances that have the Access Portal or a SIP proxy enabled or that are FireCluster members, because WatchGuard names no workaround for the three unauthenticated flaws.

records.title: CVE-2026-108142, Veeam Backup & Replication: an unauthenticated authorization bypass on the CDP Coordinator Service of 13.x backup servers (CVSS 4.0 9.1), fixed in 13.1.2 and 13.0.3, with a Backup for Microsoft 365 SQL injection to code execution and a Veeam ONE MFA bypass fixed the same day
records.headline: Veeam fixes an unauthenticated 9.1 authorization bypass on 13.x servers, a VB365 SQL injection and a ONE MFA bypass
records.summary: Veeam's advisories of 2026-10-27 fix CVE-2026-108142, an unauthenticated authorization bypass on the CDP Coordinator Service of Veeam Backup & Replication 13.1 and 13.0 on Windows and of the Veeam Software Appliance (CVSS 4.0 9.1, fixed in 13.1.2 and 13.0.3; 12.x is not affected), a SQL injection in Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 that reaches code execution as the PostgreSQL service account (9.0, fixed in 8.6) and an MFA bypass in Veeam ONE 13.1 for an attacker holding Administrator credentials (8.5). NCSC Switzerland relayed the Backup & Replication and Veeam ONE advisories on 2026-10-28 and says the vendor reports no evidence of exploitation.
actions: Upgrade every Veeam Backup & Replication 13.x server and Veeam Software Appliance to 13.1.2 (build 13.1.2.57) or 13.0.3 (build 13.0.3.63), Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 to 8.6 Patch 1 (build 8.6.0.5011) and Veeam ONE 13.1 to Patch 1 (build 13.1.0.7940), because Veeam names no workaround and warns that attackers reverse-engineer its patches.

records.title: KeyDrift: Talos reports UAT-11473 exploiting CVE-2026-20127 in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN controllers to run an implant inside the control-plane daemon that collects data-plane keys, with infrastructure overlapping Volt Typhoon's Silent Train network
records.headline: Talos: UAT-11473 implants KeyDrift in Cisco SD-WAN controllers through CVE-2026-20127 to collect data-plane keys
records.summary: Cisco Talos reports that a cluster it calls UAT-11473 exploited CVE-2026-20127, the peering authentication bypass in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, Manager and Validator (CVSS 10.0, fixed releases since February 2026, no workaround), and then ran the KeyDrift implant inside the controller's control-plane process to collect session metadata and what Talos assesses to be data-plane IPsec keys. Cisco's advisory, revised on 2026-10-28 to link Talos's post, says it is aware of limited exploitation, and Talos assesses with high confidence that the operating infrastructure overlaps considerably with Volt Typhoon's Silent Train network.
actions: Upgrade every Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, Manager and Validator to its first fixed release (20.9.8.2, 20.12.5.3 or 20.12.6.1, 20.15.4.2 or 20.18.2.1; releases earlier than 20.9 must migrate), and until then limit ports 22 and 830 on the control components to known controller and management addresses, because Cisco offers no workaround.

records.title: DeadTag: re-registered domains of defunct analytics and advertising tags redirect visitors of thousands of sites, among them to a page that serves the Coruna and DarkSword iPhone exploit kits, which compromise a vulnerable device when the page opens
records.headline: DeadTag: expired tag domains send visitors to iPhone exploit kits; opening the page is enough on vulnerable iOS
records.summary: Report URI and iVerify report that an operator they call DeadTag buys the expired domains of old analytics and advertising tags that thousands of websites still load, so every page that carries the tag runs the operator's script, and sells the visitors on; Report URI counts more than 660 re-registered domains. For chosen iPhone visitors one chain ends at a page that serves the Coruna kit to iOS 13 to 17.2.1 and a modified DarkSword kit to iOS 18.4 to 18.7, both of which attack the browser itself, so that opening the page compromises a vulnerable device and steals keychain passwords and crypto-wallet data.
actions: List every third-party script domain on the public websites your organisation, its agencies and its hosting suppliers run, and remove or re-verify each whose provider has shut down, because DeadTag buys exactly those expired domains.

records.title: CVE-2026-48356 (PolyShell), Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source: an unauthenticated file upload attacked since March 2026, fixed for supported lines in July, and listed by CISA as exploited on 2026-10-27
records.headline: PolyShell (CVE-2026-48356): Magento upload flaw attacked since March, fixed in July, CISA lists it as exploited
records.summary: Sansec reports that PolyShell, the unauthenticated file upload in the Magento and Adobe Commerce REST API that Adobe tracks as CVE-2026-48356, has been attacked since 2026-03-19, with a mass wave on 2026-03-30 that put a JavaScript loader on 471 stores in one hour. Adobe's bulletin APSB26-73 of 2026-07-14 names the 2026-jul builds as the fix and still says Adobe knows of no exploits, while Sansec says Magento 2.4.9 carried a fix on 2026-05-12; CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27. A store that ran an unpatched build may carry a webshell that the update does not remove.
actions: Update every Magento Open Source and Adobe Commerce store, those on 2.4.9 included, to the 2026-jul fix in bulletin APSB26-73, then check for compromise: any script file in the custom-options upload directory, administrator accounts nobody created and loader scripts in CMS blocks, because a store that ran an unpatched build since March 2026 may already hold a webshell that the update does not remove.

records.title: ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal (canton Bern, communal wastewater-treatment association): SafePay has put about 49 GB into the darknet, which Risikomonitor's analysis, relayed by Inside IT, finds holds personal records, bank statements, weak passwords and a third party's monitoring credentials; the association declines to comment
records.headline: Inside IT: SafePay published about 49 GB from a Bernese wastewater association; the association declines to comment
records.summary: SafePay claimed an attack on the Bernese wastewater-treatment association ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal on 2026-09-15, and Inside IT reports of 2026-10-27 that the group has now put about 49 GB of stolen data into the darknet. Risikomonitor's analysis, which Inside IT relays and which is not verified independently, finds data on more than 1,200 identifiable persons, bank statements, 255 password hits in files and a third party's monitoring-portal credentials stored on the association's server; the association will not comment, and no source says how the attackers got in.

records.headline: IDCF Cloud ransomware began with an open-source flaw in the customer portal's login system; no server data left
records.summary: IDC Frontier, a SoftBank Group subsidiary, says a ransomware attack from about 3:40 a.m. on 2026-10-07 stopped four zones of its IDCF Cloud East Japan Region 1, affecting 495 companies and local governments. Its seventh report of 2026-10-27, which closes the investigation, says an open-source flaw in the authentication system of the customer portal was exploited, after which the attacker took administrator rights on the virtualisation platform through the management console, stopped customers' virtual servers and encrypted them; it finds no trace of server data leaving, says portal registration data of up to 71 customers was queried and that backups are retrievable for 206 customers. The software is not named.

records.headline: Camping.Care booking data stolen: TCS and a second campsite warn of WhatsApp fraud; PHP link not vendor-confirmed
records.summary: TCS Camping is warning about 15,000 guests after data was stolen at Camping.Care, the Dutch supplier of the booking system for all TCS campsites; TCS confirmed the theft to SRF on 2026-10-26, SRF reports it in connection with the PHP security hole and Blick says the attackers used the two critical PHP flaws, though no source names a CVE or the entry point. Names, telephone numbers and reservation numbers are already used in fraudulent WhatsApp messages; TCS says account and IBAN data were not affected and the hole is closed. A second customer, Campingplatz Hüttenberg in canton Thurgau, has warned its guests of the same fraud in a notice that says Camping.care is still investigating the cause and does not mention PHP.

records.title: Swiss commune Manno (TI) confirms a cyberattack that encrypted part of its servers on 4 August 2026; SafePay has now published about 30 GB, which Risikomonitor reads as social-assistance decisions with AHV numbers, naturalisation files and a near-complete address book
records.headline: Inside IT: SafePay published about 30 GB from Manno, social-assistance files with AHV numbers; no commune statement
records.summary: The Ticino commune of Manno stated in a signed notice of 2026-09-16 that part of its servers were hit by an attack that encrypted data on 4 August 2026; it isolated the server and restored from existing backups. SafePay, recorded on 2026-09-28 listing manno.ch on its leak site, has since put about 30 GB of stolen data into the darknet, and Inside IT reports of 2026-10-27 that the security firm Risikomonitor found social-assistance decisions with AHV numbers and health insurers from 2014 to December 2025, debt-enforcement extracts, naturalisation files and data on the whole population of 1,381; the commune says it will make no statement.

records.title: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, NetScaler ADC and Gateway: the PHP2Shell flaws reach the management GUI on the NSIP, management-enabled SNIPs and the cluster IP of every supported version; fixed in 14.1-73.49, 13.1-64.32 and the FIPS and NDcPP builds
records.headline: NetScaler's PHP2Shell fix is out: 14.1-73.49, 13.1-64.32 and FIPS builds; restrict management access until installed
records.summary: NetScaler Product Security says the two PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 affect the NetScaler Management Portal, reached through the NSIP GUI, any SNIP that permits management access and the cluster IP GUI, on all supported software versions; NetScaler Console and SVM are not affected. Citrix's bulletin now names the fixed builds, 14.1-73.49, 13.1-64.32, 14.1-FIPS 14.1-73.49 FIPS and 13.1-FIPS and 13.1-NDcPP 13.1.37.286 and later, and tells customers to immediately restrict management access to trusted networks; no source reports an attack on NetScaler, although CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26.
actions: Install NetScaler ADC and Gateway 14.1-73.49, 13.1-64.32, 14.1-FIPS 14.1-73.49 FIPS or 13.1-FIPS and 13.1-NDcPP 13.1.37.286 (or later) on every appliance whose NSIP, a management-enabled SNIP or the cluster IP answers on its GUI or API, internet-reachable ones first; until each has its build, restrict GUI and API access on those addresses to trusted administrative hosts with ACLs, keeping NetScaler Console access working.
